There are $(n/e^2)^{n^2/6}\exp((1/2+o(1))n^{5/3})$ linear $3$-uniform hypergraphs on $[n]$, and almost all have $n^2/6-(1/6+o(1))n^{5/3}$ edges. (iii) Matroids of fixed rank. For each fixed $r\ge4$, the number $m(n,r)$ of rank-$r$ matroids on $[n]$ satisfies $\log m(n,r)=\frac{n^{r-1}}{r!}(\log n-r+1)+\left(\frac1{(r-1)!}+o(1)\right)n^{r-1-1/r}$, refining the estimates of van der Hofstad, Pendavingh and van der Pol.
item.dc:creator: Hyunwoo Lee

item.title: Forbidden subset sums in a linear range: an inverse theorem and the Erd\H{o}s-Graham irregularity problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.17205v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For $c>0$ let $f_c(n)$ be the largest size of a set $A\subseteq\{1,\dots,\lfloor cn\rfloor\}$ such that $n$ is not a sum of distinct elements of $A$. Erd\H{o}s and Graham asked whether $f_c(n)$ depends on $n$ in an irregular way (Erd\H{o}s Problem \#361). We prove that $f_c(n)=\lfloor cn\rfloor-\lceil n/2\rceil$ for $c\ge 1$, while for $0<c<1$ the ratio $f_c(n)/n$ has $\limsup$ equal to $c/2$, attained along odd $n$, and, along the integers $n$ whose least non-divisor equals a prime power $q$, tends to \[ \max\Bigl\{\frac cq,\; c-\frac12+\frac{1-c}{q}\Bigr\} \qquad\text{whenever } 2^{q-2}\min\{c,1-c\}\le 1 . \] Consequently $f_c(n)/n$ converges if and only if $c\ge1$; for $0<c<1$ it has at least two limit points, and arbitrarily many as $c\to0^+$ or $c\to1^-$. For $c=1/2$ the set of limit points is exactly $\{1/6,1/4\}$. The upper bounds follow from an inverse theorem of independent interest: if $s\ge1$, $q$ is the least positive integer not dividing $s$, and $\varepsilon>0$, then every $A\subseteq\{1,\dots,E\}$ with $|A|\ge E/q+\varepsilon T$ has a subset summing to $sT$, uniformly for all sufficiently large $T$ and all $E\le sT/2^{q-2}$. For $s=2$, this extends Alon's theorem on subsets of $\{1,\dots,N\}$ with no subset sum equal to $2N$. The results for $c\ge1$ and the $\limsup$, as well as the limits and the inverse theorem for $q\in\{2,3\}$, have been formalized and machine-checked in the Lean~4 proof assistant.
item.dc:creator: Mateo Matijasevick

item.title: Permutation patterns and higher connectivity in inversion graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.17237v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that any permutation $\pi \in S_n$ whose inversion graph is $k$-connected has at least $\frac{k+1}{2}n - C$ inversions, where $C$ depends only on $k$. In particular, inversion graphs beat the general lower bound $\frac{kn}{2}$ for the number of edges in a $k$-connected graph. Furthermore, we characterize the permutation patterns $\sigma$ having the property that if $\pi$ avoids $\sigma$, then the bound improves to $kn - C$. The collection of patterns is $\mathrm{Av}(321, 2341, 4123)$, and it is independent of $k \geq 2$. This work is motivated by a result of Linusson and Verkama (2025) that can be reinterpreted as stating that any $1324$-avoiding permutation whose inversion graph satisfies a certain weaker notion of $2$-connectivity must have at least $2n - C$ inversions. Our final result gives a characterization of the patterns having this stronger property.
item.dc:creator: Emil Verkama

item.title: Triameter, distance packings, and vertex connectivity
item.description: arXiv:2611.17259v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study upper bounds for the triameter of a connected graph in terms of distance packings and vertex connectivity. For any positive integer $k$, we bound the triameter of a graph by a linear function of its $k$-packing number and show that this bound is tight for all values of the parameters. As a corollary, we confirm the conjecture of Das and Abdio\u{g}lu on the upper bound for the triameter in terms of the order and the minimum degree of a graph. We also find the maximum triameter among graphs with given order and vertex connectivity, and describe the extremal graphs. Our main tool is a projection of a graph onto a spider or a unicyclic graph which preserves the distances between three prescribed vertices.
item.dc:creator: Artem Hak, Sergiy Kozerenko

item.title: Three-ends Furstenberg estimates and approximate rectangles
item.description: arXiv:2611.17293v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a three-ends incidence estimate whose multiplicity exponent is sharp for one-dimensional Katz-Tao point sets.} At the heart of the argument lies rectangular non-concentration and its incidence theory introduced earlier by the authors. As an application, we obtain a strong quantitative bound on the number of approximate rectangles with the vertices belonging to four separated camps, each retaining a non-concentration condition.
item.dc:creator: Ciprian Demeter, William O'Regan

item.title: Uniform Hyperbolicity of Automorphism Orbit Graphs in Rank Two
item.description: arXiv:2611.14566v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study automorphism orbit graphs of oriented conjugacy classes in the free group of rank two, with every elementary Whitehead move assigned unit cost. Collapsing signed permutations of the basis turns each orbit component into a tree of edges and triangles. We obtain this description by combining the known rank-two conjugacy-class stabilizer structure with the Bass-Serre tree of the rank-two outer automorphism group. The simplified graph and all its vertex-induced subgraphs have optimal thin-triangle constant zero for tree components and 3/4 otherwise. Every whole orbit component of the original graph has thin-triangle constant at most 2, while every component of every vertex-induced subgraph has constant at most 5/2. Both bounds are sharp in the primitive orbit and apply to the full geometric realization, including edge-interior triangle corners. The hereditary upper estimate also follows from known chordality theory; the whole-component improvement uses the geometry of adjacent permutation fibres. These results complement earlier fixed-length and minimum-length orbit classifications.
item.dc:creator: Bilal Khan

item.title: Random Chowla and Goldbach Conjectures
item.description: arXiv:2611.14579v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that for a Rademacher random multiplicative function $(f(n))_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ and any non-linear polynomial $P\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$ admitting a positive constant $\kappa_P$ such that \[\lim_{N\rightarrow\infty} \frac{\#\{n\in\left[N\right]:P(n)\text{ is square-free}\}}{N} =\kappa_P,\] we have \[ \frac{1}{\sqrt{\kappa_PN}}\sum_{n\leqslant N}f(P(n)) \xrightarrow[]{d}\mathcal{N}(0,1), \] as $N\rightarrow\infty $, where convergence is in distribution to a standard Gaussian. Using a direct combinatorial argument, we establish paucity estimates for non-trivial square products of square-free polynomial values at every fixed moment order. These estimates yield the Gaussian limit by the method of moments. We also study partial sums of the form $\sum_{n<N} F(f(n),f(N-n))$ for a suitable class of bivariate functions $F$ when $f$ is a Steinhaus random multiplicative function, and prove analogous results in special cases in the Rademacher setting. These results can be viewed as random analogues of the Goldbach-type problems considered by Mangerel.
item.dc:creator: Ihor Pylaiev

item.title: The inscribed $4$-polytope of maximal volume with ten vertices
item.description: arXiv:2611.14674v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that a $4$-polytope with ten vertices inscribed in the unit sphere $\mathbb{S}^{3}$ has volume at most $\frac{25}{384}(10 + 2\sqrt{5})$, and that, up to orthogonal transformations, equality holds only for the convex hull of two regular pentagons inscribed in $\mathbb{S}^{3}$ in orthogonal $2$-planes through the origin. As for six to nine vertices, the optimum is thus the convex hull of two regular polygons in orthogonal planes. On the combinatorial type of the pair, whose boundary complex is the join of two $5$-cycles, the sharp bound follows from our work on nine vertices. Since an optimal polytope is simplicial, by a result of Horv\'ath and L\'angi, it remains to exclude the other $162003$ simplicial types. We do this by sum-of-squares certificates checked in exact arithmetic, extended by nonnegative multiples of facet polynomials, which are positive on every positively oriented realisation of
item.dc:creator: Csaba Medgyes

item.title: Foliations, free cores, and Terao's conjecture for seventeen lines
item.description: arXiv:2611.14689v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that freeness is determined by the intersection lattice for arrangements of seventeen lines in the complex projective plane. The proof reduces a possible counterexample to smaller arrangements whose realisation spaces can be computed. A minimal logarithmic derivation defines a foliation; its inflection divisor and a local singularity count imply that the non-free member of a counterexample is nearly free with exponents $(7,10)$. Deleting four lines then produces a thirteen-line arrangement whose second Chern class is controlled by a combinatorial deficit. When the deficit is four, the remaining arrangement is free with exponents $(6,6)$. An exact covering argument places the necessary thirteen-line cores in four finite classes, containing $3{,}829{,}691$ lattices. We compute their realisation spaces and reconstruct all relevant seventeen-line extensions, including specialisations of positive-dimensional families. Among the candidate lattices, exactly sixteen admit a non-free realisation; they are rigid and have no free realisation. Together with the known cases, this establishes Terao's conjecture for central arrangements of at most seventeen planes in $\mathbb{C}^3$.
item.dc:creator: Felipe Monteiro, Henrique N. S\'a Earp, Tom\'as S. R. Silva

item.title: Exploring 3-CNF Formulas Generated From Partial Steiner Triple Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.14738v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Steiner triple systems (STS) and subsets of these known as partial STS (PSTS) are combinatorial objects that have received substantial interest from mathematicians since their introduction in 1847. Over the last three decades, (P)STS have found applications in diverse fields ranging from digital circuit testing to wireless transmission. Perhaps unsurprisingly, the triple in (P)STS allows for a mapping to 3-conjunctive normal form (3-CNF) formulas, the Boolean formula used as input to 3-SAT. Prompted by this ready conversion of (P)STS to 3-CNF formulas and numerous real-world applications of (P)STS, we explore the intersection of (P)STS with 3-SAT and its counting version \#3-SAT. We explain the properties of (P)STS-generated 3-CNF formulas in terms familiar to the SAT community and experimentally compare them against randomly-generated 3-CNF formulas. We find that PSTS-3-CNF formulas are statistically distinct from randomly generated 3-CNF formulas, in both probability of satisfiability and expected solution count.
item.dc:creator: Wyatt Olson, Jared Soundy, J. Z. Schroeder

item.title: Sign components for general bosonic-fermionic coinvariant rings
item.description:
arXiv:2611.14773v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the sign-isotypic components of the symmetric group coinvariant rings $R_n^{(k,\ell)} \otimes R_n^{(a,b)}$ and $R_n^{(k+a,\ell+b)}$ are isomorphic if and only if $n \leq 2$ or at least one of $(k,\ell)$ or $(a,b)$ is $(0,0)$ or $(0,1)$. Moreover, for $k \geq 1$ the $
u$-isotypic components $\left(R_n^{(k,\ell)} \otimes R_n^{(0,1)}ight)^
u$ and $\left(R_n^{(k,\ell+1)}ight)^
u$ are isomorphic if and only if $
u$ corresponds to the sign representation. We also show that the socle of $R_n^{(k,\ell)}$ always contains the sign component, extending one direction of a result of Haiman for $R_n^{(2,0)}$. We settle the hook components conjecture of Bergeron (2024) for coinvariant rings, and a conjecture of Bergeron (2020) that the multiplicity of the sign character of $R_n^{(1,2)}$ is $3^{n-1}$. Our results also recover several existing results in the literature. Lastly, we extend our results to the hyperoctahedral group ${\mathfrak{B}_n}$ and prove that the determinant-isotypic components of $R_{\mathfrak{B}_n}^{(k,\ell)} \otimes R_{\mathfrak{B}_n}^{(0,1)}$ and $R_{\mathfrak{B}_n}^{(k,\ell+1)}$ are isomorphic.
item.dc:creator: Nicolle Gonz\'alez, John Lentfer, Pablo S. Ocal

item.title: Hopf algebras of leaf-graded forests
item.description: arXiv:2611.14812v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We examine the relationship between the Hopf algebra on nonplanar binary forests, previously defined by the author, and a Hopf algebra defined by Bruned and used in the renormalization of stochastic PDEs. We show that Bruned's Hopf algebra and its reduced analogue, previously studied by Foissy in the context of combinatorial twisted bialgebras, are dual to Hopf algebras derived from pre-Lie insertion operations respecting the number of leaves, which induce leaf-based gradings on the dual Hopf algebras. We compute Hochschild 1-cocycles for these Hopf algebras and show that Bruned's Hopf algebra satisfies a similar universal property as the Connes-Kreimer Hopf algebra.
item.dc:creator: Elizabeth Xiao

item.title: Tripod Reordering: A 33-Queue Layout of Planar Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.14817v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A queue layout of a graph consists of a linear order of the vertices and a partition of the edges into queues so that no two edges in a single queue are nested. The minimum number of queues needed in a queue layout of a graph is called its queue number. A planar product structure theorem of Dujmovi\'c, Joret, Micek, Morin, Ueckerdt, and Wood (JACM, 2020) states that every planar graph is a subgraph of the strong product of a graph of simple treewidth at most $3$, a clique $K_3$, and a path. The result has been used to show that the queue number of planar graphs is at most $49$. Recently, Bekos, Gronemann, and Raftopoulou (Algorithmica, 2023) investigated how the general approach based on the product structure can be optimized for planar graphs. They claim that an appropriate reordering of the three vertices associated with each bag in the product structure decomposition, called a tripod, reduces the queue number of planar graphs to $42$. We first highlight a gap in their queue layout algorithm: one of the choices required by the algorithm is not guaranteed to exist. Then we show how to address the limitation and provide an alternative tripod reordering mechanism that reduces the upper bound on the queue number of planar graphs to $33$. As a corollary, bipartite planar graphs have queue number at most $22$.
item.dc:creator: Sergey Pupyrev

item.title: Geometric Combinatorics of Polynomials with Rotationally Symmetric Roots
item.description: arXiv:2611.14841v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In a recent paper by Dougherty and McCammond, the authors introduced a piecewise Euclidean cell structure for the space of monic centered polynomials. This was achieved by studying the relationship between the polynomials and their critical values, using the Lyashko-Looijenga (LL) map, as well as the noncrossing combinatorics of the polynomials. In this paper, we extend their results to the space of polynomials with rotationally symmetric roots by studying an appropriate generalisation of the LL map, which relates the polynomials and their reduced critical values. The combinatorics of the polynomials are noncrossing partitions of type $B_d$. This give us a piecewise Euclidean cell structure built using the order complex of the noncrossing partition of type $B_d$. Along the way, we also give a compactification of this space of polynomials.
item.dc:creator: Benedict Lee

item.title: Explicit Subspace Evasive Sets via Subspace Designs
item.description: arXiv:2611.14909v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Given a finite field $\mathbb F_q$, we say that a set $A\subseteq \mathbb F^n_q$ is an $(r,c)$ subspace evasive set if and only if for any affine subspace $U\subseteq \mathbb F^n_q$ with bounded dimension $\dim(U)\leq r$, the intersection size $|A\cap U|$ is at most $c$. The probabilistic method shows the existence of $(r,c)$ subspace evasive sets with $|A| = q^{(1-\epsilon) n}$ with $c = O(r/\epsilon)$. However, the best explicit constructions by Dvir--Lovett (STOC 2012) and Ben-Aroya--Shinkar (CJTCS 2013) have $c$ growing as an exponential function of $r$. Here, we give an explicit construction of such subspace evasive set that achieves the intersection bound $c=O(\min(r\log(r/\epsilon)/\epsilon, r^2/\epsilon))$ when both $r$ and $1/\epsilon$ are constants. Our approach is simple and the key idea is to compose subspace design codes (Guruswami-Xing, STOC 2013) with a suitably chosen ``local'' subspace evasive set. As a corollary, we give the first construction of an explicit (strongly) capacity-achieving list-recoverable code with nearly optimal list size, circumventing all previously-known barriers to construction.
item.dc:creator: Joshua Brakensiek, Yeyuan Chen, Mahdi Cheraghchi, Rohan Goyal, Venkatesan Guruswami, Aaron Putterman, Zihan Zhang

item.title: Face rings and the cohomology of unions of Schubert varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.15065v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The cohomology ring of a union of Schubert varieties $X_{W}=\bigcup_{w\in W}X_w,$ for $W\subseteq S_n$, in the complete flag variety is well known to be a quotient of the coinvariant ring $R_n$. We determine exactly when the ideal defining this quotient is generated by squarefree monomials, i.e. when it can be identified with the image of a Stanley-Reisner ideal $I_\Delta$ in $R_n$. We prove that a single Schubert variety $X_w$ has this property exactly when $w\in S_n$ avoids a set of seven patterns, and in this case we describe the corresponding doubly-pruned simplicial complex $\Delta$. We then show this is equivalent to $X_w$ being cut out of the complete flag variety by particular inclusion conditions on the pieces of the flag. We prove these complexes are vertex decomposable, and are Cohen-Macaulay precisely when $X_w$ is smooth. We then give a closed formula for the Poincar\'e polynomial of $X_w$. For unions $X_W$, pattern avoidance is necessary but no longer sufficient, and we prove a necessary and sufficient condition we call prunable that describes how the individual complexes associated to each $w\in W$ may be glued in the union. Quotients of $R_n$ by squarefree monomial ideals appear naturally in the Adams-Reiner conjecture on resolutions of Stanley-Reisner rings over certain parameter rings. We prove their conjecture for a family of simplicial complexes that includes the doubly-pruned complexes.
item.dc:creator: Ashleigh Adams-Jessmore, Sean T. Griffin, Tim Ryan

item.title: Congruence properties modulo powers of 3 for designated summands in partitions into odd parts
item.description: arXiv:2611.15164v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\textup{PDO}_\textup{t}(n)$ denote the total number of tagged parts over all partitions of $n$ into odd parts with designated summands. Using $3$-dissection identities and coefficient extraction, we obtain explicit polynomial expansions for the generating functions of two infinite families of arithmetic subsequences of $\textup{PDO}_\textup{t}(n)$. We establish lower bounds for the $3$-adic valuations of the coefficients in these expansions, thereby proving two infinite families of congruences modulo powers of 3 conjectured by Lin (J. Number Theory,~2018). We then estimate the $3$-adic valuations of two-by-two determinants formed from consecutive coefficient vectors. These estimates yield two infinite families of internal congruences modulo high powers of $3$.
item.dc:creator: Xingyi Li, Dazhao Tang

item.title: Growth function of the cactus groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.15249v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We determine the growth functions of the cactus groups of all degrees with respect to their standard generators, and provide explicit equations for specific degrees as examples.
item.dc:creator: Takatoshi Hama

item.title: A polynomial-time approximation scheme for the weighted Euclidean Minimum Latency Problem in fixed dimension
item.description: arXiv:2611.15425v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In the Traveling Salesman Problem, a route must visit all customers and return to its starting point while minimizing its total length. The Minimum Latency Problem, also known as the Traveling Repairman Problem, instead minimizes the sum of the times at which customers are first visited. We give a deterministic polynomial-time approximation scheme for the weighted Euclidean Minimum Latency Problem in every fixed dimension, with arbitrary nonnegative customer weights. Our proof restricts the form of a solution in three steps, each with a controlled increase in cost. First, a decomposition based on Sitters' method assigns customers to phases that start and end at the root. Second, within each phase, we divide the route into a constant number of blocks and charge each customer at the end of its assigned block. The resulting objective is a nonnegative linear combination of block lengths. Third, we add an auxiliary dimension and use a fixed Minkowski norm to close each block path into a tour. Arora's closed-tour estimate then gives paths that cross the boundaries of a common dissection only at designated portals and a bounded number of times per face. A dynamic program optimizes the restricted objective, and projecting its paths back to the original space gives the final route. Rounding weights and coordinates keeps the state space polynomial.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Skachkov, Yuriy Dorn

item.title: Solutions of the set-theoretic quantum Yang-Baxter equation arising from posets
item.description: arXiv:2611.15540v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Victoria Lebed observed that the map $(x, \, y) \mapsto (\min\{x, \, y\}, \, \max\{x, \, y\})$ on a totally ordered set is an idempotent solution of the braid equation. We extend this example in several directions, by constructing four families of solutions of the braid equation associated to posets. First, for a given poset $P$, the map $R_P$ which sorts the comparable pairs and fixes the incomparable ones is an idempotent solution of the braid equation whose automorphism group is the automorphism group of the poset $P$. Combined with the classical theorem of Birkhoff, this shows that every group is isomorphic to the automorphism group of an idempotent solution of the braid equation of the form $(P, \, R_P)$, for some poset $P$. Moreover, $R_P \cong R_Q$ if and only if $P \cong Q$, and the solutions of the form $R_P$ are exactly the idempotent solutions of the braid equation which permute the components of each pair. Secondly, we classify all the solutions $R$ of the braid equation on an arbitrary set $X$ such that $R(x, \, y) \in \{(x, \, y), \, (y, \, x)\}$ for all $x$, $y\in X$: they are exactly the solutions $R_{\mathcal{P}}$ associated to the decompositions $\mathcal{P}$ of $X$ into posets. Finally, we associate to any finite poset $P$ two involutive solutions $D_P$ and $E_P$ of the braid equation, whose automorphism groups are $(\mathbb{Z}/2)^P \rtimes {\rm Aut} (P)$ and, if $P$ is connected and has at least two elements, the group of automorphisms and anti-automorphisms of $P$.
item.dc:creator: Gigel Militaru

item.title: Specializations of frozen variables for Grassmannian cluster algebra
item.description: arXiv:2611.15611v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The homogeneous coordinate ring of a Grassmannian variety $\mathrm{Gr}_{k,n}$ is equipped with a structure of a cluster algebra. The frozen variables are identified with the Pl\"ucker coordinates corresponding to length-$k$ segments of ${\mathbb Z}_n$. We study two families of algebras: the first family is obtained by specializing all the frozen variables and the second corresponds to the specialization of the nonwrapping variables. We construct flat bases in both families and study their affine spectra. The special fibers of the families are cones over projective varieties. We identify the irreducible components of these projective varieties with certain positroid varieties.
item.dc:creator: Evgeny Feigin, Jian-Rong Li

item.title: An Empirical Square-Root Law for the Degree Discrepancy of Binary m-Sequences
item.description: arXiv:2611.15635v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $k\ge 2$, $N=2^k$, $M=N-1$ and let $\Delta(r)$ be the range, over all starting offsets, of the total-variation degree discrepancy of a length-$r$ window of a primitive binary linear feedback shift register (LFSR) of period $M$. Degree-discrepancy profiles for every $k\le 28$ support the scaling $\max_r \Delta(r)=\Theta(\sqrt{N})=\Theta(2^{k/2})$. The tabulated peaks are maxima on a discrete grid, hence lower bounds on the exhaustive maximum. The normalized peaks $d_k=\max_{r\in R_k}\Delta(r)/2^{k/2}$ oscillate between values near 1/2 and values that approach, but do not exceed, 1. The data suggest $\liminf d_k=1/2$ and $\limsup d_k\le 1$. We conjecture the same square-root law for the exhaustive maximum, with those normalized envelopes. A Brownian-bridge heuristic accounts for the square-root scale. The same profiles do not place the recorded maximizer at mid-path: after folding by the complement identity $\Delta(M-r)=\Delta(r)$, the median of $\min(\rho^*_k,1-\rho^*_k)$ is 0.35, and several $k$ (notably 16 and 28) peak on a short window. Mid-horizon $\Delta$ remains a large fraction of the peak, so the square-root scale can still come from a Brownian-bridge envelope. The same range has two readings of the starting offset: a pairing fragment in serial-knockout scheduling, and a change to the plaintext on an LFSR orbit. The location of the maximizer is not part of the conjecture. Open questions that separate the conjecture from a theorem are listed.
item.dc:creator: Joonas P\"a\"akk\"onen

item.title: Tree Decomposition of Product and Nest Graphs for Assortment Optimization under the Generalized Nested Logit Model
item.description: arXiv:2611.15817v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The generalized nested logit model extends the nested logit model by allowing each product to belong to multiple nests. The overlapping nests in the generalized nested logit model can capture complex substitution patterns, and the model has found applications in many areas. We study the assortment optimization problem under the generalized nested logit model and prove that it is NP-hard when there are only two nests or when any two distinct nests have at most one product in common. Motivated by these complexity results, we introduce novel concepts of product and nest graphs that capture which products are included in which nests. We use the tree decompositions of the graphs to characterize when the assortment optimization problem admits efficient solution methods. When the treewidth of a product graph is bounded, the assortment optimization problem can be solved in polynomial time. If the treewidth of the product graph is unbounded but the treewidth of the nest graph is bounded, then there exists a fully polynomial-time approximation scheme. These results represent the first polynomial-time algorithms for assortment optimization under the generalized nested logit model. Our numerical experiments on synthetic and real datasets show that the generalized nested logit model provides a better fit to the data than many existing models in the literature.
item.dc:creator: Yuheng Wang, Paat Rusmevichientong, Huseyin Topaloglu

item.title: Conflict-Free Cuts: Exploring the Boundaries of Tractability
item.description: arXiv:2611.15846v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A conflict-free cut of a host graph $G$ is an edge cut containing no conflicting pair of edges. The conflicts are specified by a conflict graph $\widehat G$ whose vertex set is $E(G)$. The conflict-free cut problem asks if the given instance $(G, \widehat G)$ has a conflict-free cut. When restricted to planar $G$ and 1-regular $\widehat G$, the problem is polynomial time solvable when $G$ has maximum degree 4, but NP-complete already at maximum degree 5. We study the complexity of conflict-free cut problem under restrictions on the degrees of $G$, the components of $\widehat G$, and the locality of the conflicts. A conflict is local if its two edges share an endpoint in $G$. We prove the following results. * For $\Delta(\widehat G)\le1$, a directed-cycle formulation gives a polynomial-time algorithm when $|E(G)|\le2|V(G)|$, hence for maximum degree four. The problem is NP-complete on $5$-regular hosts with exactly $1$-regular conflicts. * For $\Delta(\widehat G)\le1$, we give a constructive FPT algorithm in $s_4(G)=\sum_v\max\{0,d_G(v)-4\}$, single-exponential for planar hosts. For arbitrary conflicts, we give an XP algorithm in $\eta=\max\{0,|E(\widehat G)|-|V(G)|\}$. * On $4$-regular hosts, local exactly $2$-regular conflicts with components $C_3,C_4$ give NP-completeness. For local conflicts at maximum degree four, pair or triangle components separately permit polynomial algorithms, but mixing them gives NP-completeness. We classify cases where $\widehat G$ is a union of cliques. * An $a$-COC is a vertex set whose deletion leaves components of order at most $a$. For local conflicts, the problem is FPT in the minimum $2$-COC size, but NP-complete with a supplied $3$-COC of size six. Without locality, hardness holds with a supplied $2$-COC of size six. Both hardness results use exactly $1$-regular conflicts.
item.dc:creator: Subrahmanyam Kalyanasundaram, Subodh Kumar

item.title: Riordan Arrays as Structured Operators for Artificial Intelligence
item.description: arXiv:2611.15954v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Riordan arrays have traditionally been studied as infinite lower-triangular matrices that encode generating-function transformations and combinatorial relationships. This note proposes a complementary direction: using Riordan arrays as structured operators in artificial intelligence and data analysis. For a data sequence with generating function $A(z)$, a Riordan array $(g(z),f(z))$ produces the transformation \[ A(z)\longmapsto g(z)A(f(z)). \] This yields a parameterized family of causal linear operators that combine convolution, substitution, and multiscale mixing. The resulting structure may support parameter-efficient neural-network layers, variable-length sequence models, interpretable recurrent systems, invertible architectures, and models for hierarchical or recursively generated data. We explain what the infinite-dimensional viewpoint does and does not provide, outline several possible architectures, identify theoretical and numerical challenges, and propose an initial experimental program. The aim is not to claim that Riordan arrays are appropriate for all data, but to identify settings in which their algebraic structure supplies a useful inductive bias.
item.dc:creator: Dennis Davenport, Dewayne A. Dixon, Moussa Doumbia

item.title: The multiplicative complexity of the three-bit low-half multiplier
item.description: arXiv:2611.15992v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the multiplicative complexity of the three-bit low-half multiplier is six, giving a structural, enumeration-free lower-bound proof valid against unrestricted nonlinear reuse in Boolean XOR-AND circuits. The value was previously established by SAT searches of the second author. An explicit six-AND circuit supplies the upper bound. The lower bound combines derivatives, quadratic products, complementary minors, and extraction modulo a Boolean ideal. Independent finite checks accompany the arguments. $\mathrm{MC}(M_3)=6$ is fully formalized in Lean 4. The kernel-checked proof uses only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
item.dc:creator: Bshara Alhodali, Gregory Morse

item.title: A global rigidity criterion for Coxeter $3$-polytopes
item.description: arXiv:2611.16135v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a combinatorial condition ensuring global projective rigidity of simple hyperbolic Coxeter $3$-polytopes. As an application, we prove that every right-angled L\"obell polytope is globally rigid.
item.dc:creator: Sunghwan Ko

item.title: Congruences Modulo 16, 32 and 64 for a Restricted Overpartition Function
item.description: arXiv:2611.16145v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\overline{t}^{(3)}(n)$ denote the number of overpartitions of $n$ in which consecutive parts differ by a multiple of $3$ unless the larger part is overlined, and the smallest part is overlined unless it is divisible by $3$. Using dissections of theta functions, we establish two infinite families of congruences modulo $32$ and $64$. We also obtain two residue formulas modulo $16$ and use them to derive four further infinite families of congruences modulo $16$. In particular, for every positive integer $M$ and nonnegative integer $n$, the residue of $\overline{t}^{(3)}(M^2(18n+12))$ modulo $16$ is $8$ if $6n+4$ is a square and $0$ otherwise.
item.dc:creator: Li Zhang, Qiao-Mei Zhang

item.title: A Polynomial Bound on Split Rank
item.description: arXiv:2611.16231v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the split rank of a rational pure-integer polyhedron is polynomially bounded in its input length, resolving a conjecture of Basu, Conforti, Di Summa, and Jiang. If the defining system has dense binary encoding length $L$, then $O((L+1)^9)$ split rounds suffice to reach the integer hull in arbitrary dimension.
item.dc:creator: Avinash Bhardwaj, Vishnu Narayanan

item.title: On the $h$-polynomials of cyclotomic standard graded Cohen-Macaulay rings
item.description: arXiv:2611.16362v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We say that a standard graded algebra is cyclotomic if all roots of its $h$-polynomial lie on the complex unit circle. We study which products of cyclotomic polynomials can occur as $h$-polynomials of standard graded Cohen--Macaulay algebras without being of complete intersection type. For each fixed positive integer $a$, we reduce the nonexistence problem for multiplicities $ap$ over all sufficiently large primes $p$ to finitely many cases. Combining this reduction with explicit constructions, we completely characterize the positive integers $k$ for which such a polynomial of multiplicity $8k$ exists: precisely those satisfying \[k\notin\{1,2,3,6\}\cup\{p:p\ge7\text{ is prime}\}\cup\{3p:p\ge17\text{ is prime}\}.\]
item.dc:creator: Akihiro Higashitani, Takumi Yanagida

item.title: Continuous representations of topological monoids via reconstruction
item.description: arXiv:2611.16436v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study continuous representations of topological monoids on discrete modules via a finite-restriction reconstruction method. For an arbitrary topological monoid $\mathscr{M}$, we construct a transformation monoid $\mathscr{E}_\mathscr{M}$ whose uniformly continuous representations are equivalent to continuous representations of $\mathscr{M}$ on discrete modules. By the finite-restriction reconstruction, these categories are equivalent to categories of sheaves of modules over special sites. We illustrate this method by several examples, including various realizations of $\mathrm{FA}$-modules and continuous representations of $\operatorname{End}_A(\varinjlim_r A^r)$ for a finite ring $A$.
item.dc:creator: Zhenxing Di, Liping Li, Li Liang

item.title: Complete enumeration of maximal T-curves in degrees eight and nine
item.description: arXiv:2611.16659v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We use a highly parallelized backtracking algorithm implemented in CUDA to enumerate every compatible collection of Harnack splits in degrees eight and nine. By a theorem of Haas (1997) this yields every maximal T-curve. In this way, we find that exactly 38 real schemes of real plane algebraic curves of degree eight with 22 real components and 225 of degree nine with 29 real components are realized by combinatorial patchworking.
item.dc:creator: Zoe Geiselmann, Michael Joswig, Lars Kastner, Marcel Wack

item.title: On the randomized lattice-point count problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.16769v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Counting (integer) lattice points in a convex body $K$ has a rich history, beginning with the famous circle problem imposed by Gauss in 1834. Clearly, the number of covered lattice points depends on the position, orientation, size, and shape of $K$ in a delicate way. In 1947, Kendall was the first to consider a randomized version of this problem by allowing random translations of $K$. In this survey, we aim to provide an overview of the current state of research on the \emph{randomized lattice-point count problem}, i.e.\ on the distribution of the lattice-point count under random rotations and translations of $K$. As it turns out, even the variance is far from being well-understood, leaving multiple open questions for future research. The motivation for the present work grew out of the author's research interest in a related combinatorial problem, dealing with the convex hull of all covered lattice points.
item.dc:creator: Steffen Schlie

item.title: Novel upper bounds for Borsuk numbers from contact points and spherical partitions
item.description: arXiv:2611.16775v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $b(n)$ be the least $m$ such that every bounded set in $\mathbb{R}^n$ of positive diameter can be partitioned into $m$ sets of smaller diameter. We prove that \[ b(4)\le6,\qquad b(5)\le12,\qquad b(6)\le31,\qquad b(7)\le45,\qquad b(8)\le89, \] and that \[ b(n)\le1+2^{n-1}\left(\tfrac{39}{64}\right)^{\lfloor(n-1)/8\rfloor} \qquad\text{for every } n\ge9 ; \] for instance, $b(9)\le157$ and $b(17)\le24337$. Further constructions give, for example, $b(10)\le289$ and $b(13)\le2313$. These bounds improve Lassak's bound $b(n)\le2^{n-1}+1$ of 1982 in every dimension $n\ge4$. In dimension four they also improve the recent bounds $b(4)\le8$ (Tolmachev and Voronov, May 2026) and $b(4)\le7$ (Arman, Bondarenko, Prymak and Radchenko, October 2026); the bound $b(4)\le6$ was announced independently by Chalmers in November 2026. The bounds for $n\ge7$ have analytic proofs: a quantitative form of Lassak's reduction to coverings of the sphere is combined with normal partitions of weighted vector configurations, for which the smallest inner product within a region is estimated explicitly. The bound for $n=6$ uses a covering of $S^4$ by thirty sets, checked in rational arithmetic. For $n=4,5$ three contact points of the circumscribed ball reduce the problem to a four-parameter family of bodies, which is split by finitely many power diagrams; that all parts have diameter less than one is verified by a computer program with rigorous error control.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Tolmachev

item.title: Congruences involving the products of three binomial coefficients II
item.dc:creator: Zhi-Hong Sun

item.title: Constrained intersection representations and forbidden patterns
item.description: arXiv:2611.16849v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the interplay between two types of graph classes: the ones defined by intersections of geometric objects and the ones defined by the absence of a substructure. More precisely, we study intersection graphs that are grounded, that is, the objects lie above a horizontal line that they touch, and ordered graphs with forbidden patterns, that is, ordered graphs that avoid a set of ordered induced subgraphs. These two approaches are fundamentally different, but it is known that several interesting graph classes have both types of characterizations, and we aim to understand whether this is a general phenomenon. Our contributions are the following. First, we identify a family of patterns on four vertices and a natural hierarchy of intersection graphs of strings whose classes are nicely interleaved. This raises hopes to prove connections between the two perspectives. Second, we dampen these hopes by proving that a class of (ordered) intersection graphs that we study cannot be characterized by a finite set of forbidden patterns. Third, we show a dual impossibility result: there exists a pattern-defined class of our hierarchy that admits no intersection representation, if we require this representation to be closed under natural operations such as translation and scaling. However, it turns out that if we allow slightly more exotic intersection representations, then we can find one for this pattern-defined class.
item.dc:creator: Laurent Feuilloley, Michel Habib, Amalia Sorondo

item.title: Covering the Square Lattice and the Honeycomb with Non-Overlapping Unit Disks
item.description: arXiv:2611.16894v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For $d>0$, let $\mathcal{S}_d$ be the square lattice and $\mathcal{H}_d$ the honeycomb point set with minimum distance $d$. We study for which $d$ these sets can be covered by closed unit disks with pairwise disjoint interiors; the periodic constructions of Phetmak, Nuntasombat and Fakcharoenphol cover them only from $d=1/2$ and $d=2/\sqrt{37}$ on, with gaps. Writing $\mathcal{N}(d)$ for the largest number of points in a closed unit disk and $\rho$ for the number of points per unit area, we show that neither set can be covered when $\mathcal{N}(d)<2\sqrt3\,\rho$, and we determine these spacings exactly, thirteen intervals for $\mathcal{S}_d$ and twelve for $\mathcal{H}_d$. At their right endpoints the bound is attained; there $\mathcal{S}_d$ is never coverable, and $\mathcal{H}_d$ is not coverable at nine of the twelve endpoints. We also give new periodic coverings, of $\mathcal{S}_d$ at $d=2/\sqrt{34}$ and of $\mathcal{H}_d$ for $2/9\le d\le1/\sqrt{19}$. Consequently, the smallest coverable spacing lies in $(0.2581,\,2/\sqrt{34}]$ for the square lattice and in $(0.1781,\,2/9]$ for the honeycomb point set, and coverability is not monotone in $d$ for either set.
item.dc:creator: Teeradej Kittipassorn, Nattawut Phetmak, Kirati Sriamorn

item.title: Edge-wise Graph Alignments
item.description: arXiv:2611.16901v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Pairwise graph ``alignments'', usually defined as maximum common subgraphs, have been considered in many application domains, including the comparison of molecular structures. Most commonly, the problem is formulated as maximum common induced subgraph (MCIS) or maximum common edge subgraph (MCES) problems. Sometimes these formulations are restricted to connected common subgraphs. Common subgraph problems readily generalize to more than two input graphs. However, this concept is fundamentally distinct from the notion of multiple sequence alignments. Abstractly, alignments are defined as super-structures from which the individual input objects are recovered via structure-preserving projections. While the mathematical construction readily applies to common induced subgraphs, it does not fully encompass the common edge subgraph problem, which is the variant more commonly employed in cheminformatics applications. In order to consistently define multiple edge-based alignments of graphs we represent a graph $G$ as E-graph $(E,\mathscr{V})$, where $E$ is the edge set of $G$ and $\mathscr{V}$ is the set of sets of incident edges. This representation implicitly encodes the vertices in terms of edge data. Alignments of E-graphs are themselves E-graphs that contain the input (E-)graphs as subgraphs. Maximum edge subgraphs correspond to maximum induced sub-E-graphs, and they can thus be computed using a slightly modified version of the VF2 algorithm without the need to switch from graphs to line graphs. Furthermore, multiple alignments of (E-)graphs yield a natural definition of a consensus graph that is ``on average'' present in the input without having to be a subgraph of every (and in fact of any) input graph.
item.dc:creator: Akbar Davoodi, Christoph Flamm, Daniel Merkle, Peter F. Stadler

item.title: Poincar\'e polynomials of nilmanifolds associated with path graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.17014v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give explicit and recursive formulas for the Poincar\'e polynomials of Dani--Mainkar nilmanifolds associated with path graphs. We also prove that these polynomials are unimodal, and we calculate a range of Betti numbers asymptotically. As an application, we derive a sharp lower bound for the dimension of the total de Rham cohomology of a Dani--Mainkar nilmanifold.
item.dc:creator: Marco Aldi, Samuel Bevins, Eleftherios Chatzitheodoridis, Sergio Da Silva, Quincy Frias, Tom\'as Mej\'ia G\'omez

item.title: On the multidimensional polynomial Szemer\'{e}di theorem
item.description: arXiv:2611.17136v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the multidimensional polynomial Szemer\'{e}di theorem over prime fields. Let $P_1,\dots,P_m\in\F_p[t]^k$ be block independent vector polynomials of degree at most $d$, with $P_i(0)=0$ for every $i$. We prove that there is a constant $c=c(k,m,d)>0$ such that, for every sufficiently large prime $p$, every set $A\subset\F_p^k$ with $|A|\ge p^{k-c}$ contains a configuration $x,x+P_1(t),\dots,x+P_m(t)$ with $t\in\F_p\setminus\{0\}$.
item.dc:creator: Danqing He, Xuancheng Shao

item.title: Algebraic and geometric aspects of Demazure weaves
item.description: arXiv:2611.17155v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: These are notes to supplement my talks at the Current Developments in Mathematics Conference in 2026. They are an expository account of recent work in the study of braid varieties and their relation to low-dimensional contact and symplectic topology. A driving theme is the development and use of Demazure weaves to construct cluster algebra structures on the coordinate rings of such braid varieties.
item.dc:creator: Roger Casals

item.title: Patterns, Distances, and Structure in Sparse Sets
item.description: arXiv:2611.17198v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A central theme in modern harmonic analysis, with strong connections to Ramsey theory, is the tension between randomness and structure: to what extent can a "large" set avoid prescribed configurations, and when must such patterns inevitably appear? The answer depends delicately on how size is measured, with notions such as Hausdorff dimension, Fourier dimension, and density leading to strikingly different phenomena. In this mini-course, we explore this theme through two complementary perspectives. On one hand, we study translation-invariant linear patterns, a natural class of Euclidean Ramsey-type configurations. On the other hand, we investigate distance sets of sparse subsets of Euclidean space, which encode metric configurations of pairs of points. Together, these results illustrate a unifying principle: while sparse sets may avoid individual configurations, sufficiently strong analytic or geometric conditions enforce the emergence of Ramsey-type structure. The course will emphasize key ideas, methods, and examples, aiming to provide an accessible entry point to current developments at the interface of harmonic analysis, geometric measure theory, and Euclidean Ramsey theory. Lectures are by Malabika Pramanik.
item.dc:creator: Paige Bright

item.title: Sowing the Seeds of Intractability: Kalah is PSPACE-complete
item.description: arXiv:2611.17252v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Kalah is a classic two-player game in the mancala family of sowing games. Computers have solved several standard-size starting positions, but the complexity of the game on boards of growing size has remained open. We study the natural generalization in which the number of pits per side is part of the input and an arbitrary position is given, with the stone counts given in unary. We show that deciding whether a designated player can force a win from such a position is PSPACE-complete. The hard positions have Alice to move first and both stores initially empty. The same positions are hard under either common convention for capture opposite an empty pit, and with or without the bonus rule, which gives a player another turn when the last stone is sown into their own store. We introduce Line Kalah as an intermediate problem, a game on a line in which stones that leave the line effectively disappear and Alice must save each of her target pits before Bob captures it, and we reduce quantified Boolean formulas to it. The reduction uses a set of sequential timer piles whose last stones approach a group of targets, forcing Alice to choose between two captures in order to set the truth value of a variable, and a final capture gadget to test a clause chosen by Bob (only one is needed adversarially). Since either player may move any pile at any time, the stages are placed so that premature timer firings protect earlier potential targets. For a true formula, Alice's strategy against arbitrary opposing play either gains enough time to save the remaining targets (after Bob deviates from the intended play) or reaches the final test with a correctly encoded, protected input. Finally, the line positions are embedded in Kalah with both stores empty. A separate Bob pit holds the score adjustment, so the winner takes a strict majority of the stones.
item.dc:creator: Ethan Dickey, Ethan Mader

item.title: The q-WZ Method for Infinite Series
item.description: arXiv:0806.2491v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Motivated by the telescoping proofs of two identities of Andrews and Warnaar, we find that infinite q-shifted factorials can be incorporated into the implementation of the q-Zeilberger algorithm in the approach of Chen, Hou and Mu to prove nonterminating basic hypergeometric series identities. This observation enables us to extend the q-WZ method to identities on infinite series. As examples, we will give the q-WZ pairs for some classical identities such as the q-Gauss sum, the $_6\phi_5$ sum, Ramanujan's $_1\psi_1$ sum and Bailey's $_6\psi_6$ sum.
item.dc:creator: William Y. C. Chen, Ernest X. W. Xia

item.title: The Multipartite Ramsey numbers $m_j(C_3, C_m, n_1K_2,n_2K_2,\ldots, n_iK_2)$
item.description: arXiv:2109.12210v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Assume that $K_{j\times n}$ be a complete, multipartite graph consisting of $j$ partite sets and $n$ vertices in each partite set. For given graphs $G_1, G_2,\ldots, G_n$, the multipartite Ramsey number (M-R-number) $m_j(G_1, G_2, \ldots,G_n)$ is the smallest integer $t$ such that for any $n$-edge-coloring $(G^1,G^2,\ldots, G^n)$ of the edges of $K_{j\times t}$, $G^i$ contains a monochromatic copy of $G_i$ for at least on $i$. C. J. Jayawardene, E. T. Baskoro et al. $(2016)$ gave the size of M-R-numbe $m_j(nK_2, C_7)$ for $j \geq 2 $ and $n\leq 6$. Y. Rowshan et al. $(2021)$ gave the size of M-R-number $m_j(nK_2, C_7)$ for $j = 2,3, 4$ and $n\geq 2$. Y. Rowshan $(2021)$ gave the size of M-R-number $m_j(nK_2,C_7)$, for each $j\geq 5$ and $n\geq 2$. In this article we compute the size of M-R-number $m_j(C_3,C_3, nK_2)$ for each $j\geq 7$, $n\geq 1$, $m_j(C_3,C_3, n_1K_2,n_2K_,\ldots,n_iK_2)$ for each $2\leq j\leq 6$, $i\geq 2, n_i\geq 1$, and M-R-number $m_j(C_3,C_4, nK_2)$, for each $n\geq 1$, and small $j$.
item.dc:creator: Yaser Rowshan

item.title: Hankel Determinants for Weighted Lattice Paths with Two Horizontal Steps
item.description: arXiv:2409.18609v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We evaluate all Hankel determinants of the formal power series \(G=a/(1+b_1x+b_2x^2+cx^kG)\), where \(k\ge4\). The defining equation arises from a weighted lattice-path model with horizontal steps of lengths one and two. For \(k=4\), the determinants are expressed through Fibonacci polynomials. For \(k\ge5\), explicit formulas describe each residue class of the determinant size modulo \(k\). The proofs combine quadratic transformations with a second-order recurrence for an auxiliary family. As an application, we recover known Hankel evaluations for the square of the weighted Motzkin generating function.
item.dc:creator: Ying Wang, Zihao Zhang

item.title: Combinatorics of generalized orthogonal polynomials of type $R_{II}$
item.description: arXiv:2411.12345v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In 1995, Ismail and Masson introduced orthogonal polynomials of types \( R_I \) and \( R_{II} \), which are defined by specific three-term recurrence relations with additional conditions. Recently, Kim and Stanton found a combinatorial interpretation for the moments of orthogonal polynomials of type \( R_I \) in the spirit of the combinatorial theory of orthogonal polynomials due to Flajolet and Viennot. In this paper, we push this combinatorial model further to orthogonal polynomials of type \( R_{II} \). Moreover, we generalize orthogonal polynomials of type \( R_{II} \) by relaxing some of their conditions. We then prove a master theorem, which generalizes combinatorial models for moments of various types of orthogonal polynomials: classical orthogonal polynomials, Laurent biorthogonal polynomials, and orthogonal polynomials of types \( R_I \) and \( R_{II} \).
item.dc:creator: Jang Soo Kim, Minho Song

item.title: Low-degree colorings without non-essential arguments
item.description: arXiv:2412.04461v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For the Hamming graph $H(n,q)$, where $q$ is a constant prime power and $n$ grows, we construct perfect colorings without non-essential arguments such that $n$ depends exponentially on the off-diagonal part of the quotient matrix. In particular, we construct unbalanced functions (in the case $q=2$, Boolean functions) such that the number of essential arguments depends exponentially on the degree of the function. Another framing of the main construction is that it gives a sequence of very regular functions (perfect colorings) whose number of essential arguments grows exponentially with respect to sensitivity. A classical result that connects sensitivity with the number of essential arguments in the binary ($q=2$) case is the Simon--Wegener theorem. We prove an analog of this theorem for an arbitrary $q$. Keywords: boolean functions, perfect colorings, equitable partitions, degree, sensitivity, essential arguments
item.dc:creator: Denis S. Krotov

item.title: Boolean combinations of graphs
item.description: arXiv:2412.19551v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Boolean combinations allow combining given combinatorial objects to obtain new, potentially more complicated, objects. In this paper, we initiate a systematic study of this idea applied to graphs. In order to understand expressive power and limitations of boolean combinations in this context, we investigate how they affect different combinatorial and structural properties of graphs, in particular $\chi$-boundedness, as well as characterize the structure of boolean combinations of graphs from various classes.
item.dc:creator: Sarosh Adenwalla, Samuel Braunfeld, John Sylvester, Viktor Zamaraev

item.title: Unavoidable subgraphs in Ramsey graphs
item.description: arXiv:2502.09830v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study subgraphs that appear in large Ramsey graphs for a given graph $F$. The recent girth Ramsey theorem of the first two authors asserts that there are Ramsey graphs such that all small subgraphs lie in `forests of copies of $F$' amalgamated on vertices and edges. We derive a few further consequences from this structural result and investigate to what extent such forests of copies must be present in Ramsey graphs. As an application, we improve a recent result on generalised Sidon sets with Ramsey-type properties.
item.dc:creator: Christian Reiher, Vojt\v{e}ch R\"odl, Mathias Schacht

item.title: The threshold for loose Hamilton cycles in random hypergraph
item.description: arXiv:2503.05121v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that w.h.p.\ the random $r$-uniform hypergraph $H_{n,m}$ contains a loose Hamilton cycle, provided $r\geq 3$ and $m\geq \frac{(1+\epsilon)n\log n}{r}$, where $\epsilon$ is an arbitrary positive constant. This is asymptotically best possible, as if $m\leq \frac{(1-\epsilon)n\log n}{r}$ then w.h.p.\ $H_{n,m}$ contains isolated vertices.
item.dc:creator: Alan Frieze, Xavier Perez-Gimenez

item.title: Perfect weight divisibility of (fork, co-fork$\cup K_1$)-free graphs
item.description: arXiv:2505.04429v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A {\em fork} is a graph obtained from $K_{1,3}$ (usually called {\em claw}) by subdividing an edge once, an {\em co-fork} is the complement graph of a fork, and a {\em co-cricket} is a union of $K_1$ and $K_4-e$. A graph is perfectly divisible if for each of its induced subgraphs $H$, $V (H)$ can be partitioned into $A$ and $B$ such that $H[A]$ is perfect and $\omega(H[B]) < \omega(H)$. A graph is perfectly weight divisible if the same condition holds for any positive integer weights on its vertices, using the maximum weight of a clique instead of the clique number. Sivaraman proposed the conjecture that every fork-free graph is perfectly divisible in a paper by Karthick {\em et al.} [Electron. J. Comb. 29 (2022), P3.19.]. In the same paper, they proved that every ((\text{fork},\text{co-cricket}))-free graph is either claw-free or perfectly divisible. In this paper, we show that every (fork, co-fork$\cup K_1$)-free graph is perfectly weight divisible, and hence perfectly divisible. This improves some results of Karthick {\em et al.}.
item.dc:creator: Ran Chen, Baogang Xu, Miaoxia Zhuang

item.title: Webification of symmetry classes of plane partitions
item.description: arXiv:2508.16565v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Webs are graphical objects that give a tangible, combinatorial way to compute and classify tensor invariants. Recently, Gaetz, Pechenik, Pfannerer, Striker, and Swanson found a rotation-invariant web basis for $\mathrm{SL}_4$, as well as its quantum deformation $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_4)$, and a bijection between move equivalence classes of $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_4)$-webs and fluctuating tableaux such that web rotation corresponds to tableau promotion. They also found a bijection between the set of plane partitions in an $a\times b\times c$ box and a benzene move equivalence class of $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_4)$-webs by determining the corresponding oscillating tableau. In this paper, we similarly find the oscillating tableaux corresponding to plane partitions in certain symmetry classes. We furthermore give a combinatorial map, defined on the span of the invariants of webs arising from certain symmetry classes, from $U_q(\sl_4)$ invariants to $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_r)$ invariants for $r=2,3$.
item.dc:creator: Ashleigh Adams, Jessica Striker

item.title: On identity Seidel switches
item.description: arXiv:2601.04530v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An identity Seidel switch of a graph is a vertex subset whose Seidel switch produces an isomorphic graph. We distinguish the elementary abelian group of switching operations from the family of identity switches of a fixed graph, which need not be a group. We obtain an edge-count condition for identity switches and deduce that every vertex-identity switch has degree half the number of remaining vertices. In particular, no graph of order at least two has every vertex as an identity switch. For a two-vertex switching set inducing an edge, we characterize the switches admitting an isomorphism that preserves the endpoint pair, in terms of automorphisms of the remaining induced subgraph. We establish modification results under this additional hypothesis and give explicit constructions of identity switches. Counterexamples show why edge-count conditions and unrestricted modification assertions do not suffice.
item.dc:creator: Severino V. Gervacio

item.title: Reconstructing a giant component of a point set in $\mathbb{R}$
item.description: arXiv:2602.23122v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $V \subset \mathbb{R}$ be a finite set with $|V| = n $ and suppose we are given each pairwise distance independently with probability $p$. We show that if $p = (1+\epsilon)/n$, for some fixed $\epsilon >0$, then we can reconstruct a subset of size $\Omega_{\epsilon}(n)$, up to translation and reflection, with high probability. This confirms a conjecture posed by Gir\~ao, Illingworth, Michel, Powierski, and Scott. We also study a deterministic variant proposed by Benjamini and Tzalik. We show that if we are given $m$ distinct pairwise distances of a point set $V \subset \mathbb{R}$ with $|V|=n$, then we can reconstruct a subset of size $\Omega(m/ (n \log n)) $, up to translation and reflection. Moreover, we show that this is optimal, which also disproves a conjecture posed by Benjamini and Tzalik.
item.dc:creator: Julien Portier

item.title: Some properties of minimally nonperfectly divisible graphs
item.description: arXiv:2603.01967v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A graph is perfectly divisible if every induced subgraph $H$ admits a partition $(A,B)$ of $V(H)$ such that $H[A]$ is perfect and $\omega(H[B])<\omega(H)$. A graph is minimally nonperfectly divisible if it is not perfectly divisible but every proper induced subgraph is perfectly divisible. We prove that every $P_2\cup P_4$-free or diamond-free minimally nonperfectly divisible graph has no homogeneous set, and that every $2P_3$-free or claw-free minimally nonperfectly divisible graph has no clique cutset. We also study the relationship between perfect divisibility and its weighted analogue, perfect weight divisibility, defined for positive integral vertex weights. We prove that if a graph $H$ has no adjacent twins, then every $H$-free graph is perfectly divisible if and only if every $H$-free graph is perfectly weight divisible.
item.dc:creator: Qiming Hu, Baogang Xu, Miaoxia Zhuang

item.title: A characterization of interval nest digraphs
item.description: arXiv:2603.08585v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A digraph consisting of a set of vertices $V$ and a set of arcs $E$ is called an interval digraph if there exists a family of closed intervals $\{I_u,J_u\}_{u \in V}$ such that $uv$ is an arc if and only if the intersection of $I_u$ and $J_v$ is non-empty. Interval digraphs naturally generalize interval graphs, by extending the classical interval intersection model to directed graphs. Several subclasses of interval digraphs have been studied in the literature-such as balanced, chronological and catch interval digraphs-each characterized by admitting interval representations that satisfy specific restrictions. Among these, interval nest digraphs are the ones that admit an interval representation in which $J_u$ is contained in $I_u$ for all vertices $u$ of $V$. In this work, we provide a complete characterization of interval nest digraphs in terms of vertex linear orderings with forbidden patterns, which we call nest orderings. This result completes the picture of vertex-ordering characterizations among the main subclasses of interval digraphs.
item.dc:creator: Ayel\'en Alcantar, Flavia Bonomo, Guillermo Dur\'an, Nina Pardal

item.title: Diagonal parity and loop toggling for symmetric matrices over $\mathbb F_2$
item.description: arXiv:2605.11056v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a symmetric matrix $M$ over $\mathbb F_2$, it is known that its diagonal vector belongs to its column space. We prove the parity refinement that every solution of $Mx=\operatorname{diag}(M)$ satisfies $\operatorname{diag}(M)^Tx\equiv\operatorname{rank}(M)\pmod 2$. This extends the parity theorem for odd dominating sets to graph matrices with arbitrary binary diagonal labels. A self-contained rank-one update formula gives the changes caused by a single loop toggle and yields $\operatorname{nul} A(\overline G)=\operatorname{nul}(A(G)+I)+[\operatorname{rank}(A(G)+I)\text{ is odd}]$. For rooted trees, we augment Filmus's three classes of realizable boundary data with an explicit multiplicity recursion. The resulting formula computes the nullity of $A(T)+D_\varepsilon$ in a single traversal and gives a nonsingularity criterion. For complete rooted trees with eventually periodic labels indexed by height above the leaves, we obtain eventual periodicity of the boundary states and nullity formulas affine in powers of the branching degree on each eventual residue class. Constant labels give explicit closed forms.
item.dc:creator: Mohsen Aliabadi

item.title: Triangle Families with Large Edge Up-Laplacian Spectral Gap
item.description: arXiv:2605.27307v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathcal{T}$ be a finite nonempty family of $3$-element sets, viewed as the triangles of a $2$-dimensional simplicial complex, and let $\lambda(\mathcal{T})$ be the smallest positive eigenvalue of its edge up-Laplacian $\delta_{1,\mathcal{T}}^T\delta_{1,\mathcal{T}}$, where $\delta_{1,\mathcal{T}}$ is the signed edge-triangle incidence matrix. We view $\lambda(\mathcal{T})$ as an analogue of the algebraic connectivity one dimension up, and study the extremal function $\phi(t)=\max_{|\mathcal{T}|=t}\lambda(\mathcal{T})$. For every $n \geq 3$, we show that $\lambda(\mathcal{T}) \leq n-1$ whenever $|\mathcal{T}|<\binom{n}{3}$ and that $\phi\left(\binom{n}{3}\right)=n$, attained only by the complete triple system on $n$ points. For every $n\geq 5$, we show that $\phi(t) \leq n-1$ for all $\binom{n}{3} < t < \binom{n+1}{3}$. In particular, $\phi$ is not monotone, while $\max_{s \leq t} \phi(s)=\max\left\{n : \binom{n}{3} \leq t \right\}$. We also prove that $\phi(t)=\Theta(t^{\frac{1}{3}}).$ The proofs rest on two local bounds: $\lambda(\mathcal{T}) \leq d+2$ for every edge lying in exactly $d$ triangles of $\mathcal{T}$, and, in the spirit of Garland's local-to-global method, $\lambda(\mathcal{T}) \leq 1 + \mu$ for every nonzero Laplacian eigenvalue $\mu$ of every connected component of every vertex link. Applying Fiedler's inequality between algebraic connectivity and minimum degree to the link, the second bound gives rigidity: an edge lying in exactly $d$ triangles with $\lambda(\mathcal{T}) > d+1$ must lie in a complete triple system on $d+2$ points that shares no edge with the rest of $\mathcal{T}$. When $\mathcal{T}$ is the set of all triangles of a connected graph, the smallest positive eigenvalue of the Helmholtzian (edge Hodge Laplacian) is the minimum of $\lambda(\mathcal{T})$ and the algebraic connectivity, so both bounds apply to it.
item.dc:creator: Mutasim Mim

item.title: Contraction Containment in Labeled Trees: Support Counts, Collision Cores, and Star Avoidance
item.description: arXiv:2606.07668v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study whether a labeled tree can be recovered from the numbers of larger labeled trees that contract to it. We first characterize containment using the edge splits induced on a proposed survivor set and derive an exact formula for hosts with one marked display. We then study several displays in the same host. After contracting every edge invisible to all \(k\) displays of an \(n\)-vertex target, the remaining collision core has at most \(k(n-1)+1\) vertices. Once the coincidences and relative positions of the surviving labels are recorded, these bounded cores give a finite exact expansion of each collision count. We also prove that almost every sufficiently large labeled tree contains any fixed target, with an exponentially small exceptional proportion. We obtain an exact avoidance formula and generating function for star displays in which the center survivor is the largest label of the host. We call such displays top-centered. We derive fixed-star asymptotics and a coarse threshold for this restricted containment problem.
item.dc:creator: Levi Segal

item.title: Normal ordering in the $(p,q)$-deformed generalized Weyl algebra. I: Algebraic Framework and Combinatorial Identities
item.description: arXiv:2606.22585v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The $(p,q)$-deformed generalized Weyl algebra is generated by variables $X, Y$ and $Z_p$ which satisfy the commutation relations $XY-qYX=h Y^sZ_{p}, XZ_p=pZ_pX$, and $Z_pY=pYZ_p$, with $s\in \mathbb{N}_0$ and where $p^s=1$. We investigate the problem of normal ordering arbitrary words in these letters with the help of Young diagrams, and we treat certain special cases explicitly. In particular, the connection to generalized Stirling numbers is considered in detail.
item.dc:creator: Toufik Mansour, Lahcen Oussi, Matthias Schork

item.title: A unified approach to cross-intersection problems with applications to Hilton--Milner type theorems and stability
item.description: arXiv:2607.03315v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a new approach to cross-intersection problems in extremal set theory. The method builds on the iterative procedure introduced by Kupavskii and Zakharov (2024) and the $t$-cover method. It provides a flexible framework for deriving extremal and stability results for cross $t$-intersecting families. Our approach applies to a variety of combinatorial objects. As an application, we prove a product version of the seminal Erd\H{o}s--Ko--Rado theorem for sufficiently spread set systems. Two families $\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{G}$ of $k$-subsets of $[n]$ are called cross $t$-intersecting if $|F\cap G|\geq t$ for all $F\in\mathcal{F}$ and $G\in\mathcal{G}$. We determine the families maximizing $\min\{|\mathcal{F}|, |\mathcal{G}|\}$ for large $n$ and all $t\ge2$, generalizing results of M\"{o}rs (1985) and F\"{u}redi (1995) for cross $1$-intersecting families. We then determine the families maximizing $|\mathcal{F}||\mathcal{G}|$ under the condition $\max\{|\cap_{F\in\mathcal{F}}F|,|\cap_{G\in\mathcal{G}}G|\}<t$ for large $n$. This improves the bound obtained by Frankl and Wang (2024), and provides a characterization of extremal configurations. For a family $\mathcal{F}$ of subsets of $[n]$, we introduce its $t$-diversity $\gamma_t(\mathcal{F})$, defined as the minimum number of sets from $\mathcal{F}$ not containing a fixed $t$-subset. This serves as a natural generalization of the important notion of diversity for $t=1$. We obtain a stability result via $\gamma_t$, and determine the maximum of $\min\{\gamma_t(\mathcal{F}),\gamma_t(\mathcal{G})\}$ for cross $t$-intersecting families $\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{G}$. These yield new results for $t$-intersecting families, including a stability theorem towards a conjecture of Ellis, Keller and Lifshitz (2019), which may also be regarded as a $t$-intersection version, for large $n$, of an influential theorem of Frankl (1987).
item.dc:creator: Jie Wen, Benjian Lv

item.title: Lin--Lu--Yau Curvature and Edge-Connectivity of Hypergraphs
item.description: arXiv:2608.06029v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a local geometric criterion ensuring that the edge-connectivity of a hypergraph equals its minimum incidence degree: every locally finite connected simple $r$-uniform linear hypergraph with $r\ge3$ and nonnegative Lin--Lu--Yau curvature has this property. Among the various extensions of Ollivier--Ricci curvature to hypergraphs, we work with the equal-edges random walk on hypergraphs \cite{CoupetteEtAl2023}. Moreover, we show that both uniformity and linearity are essential: if either assumption is removed, there exist positively curved hypergraphs for which the gap between minimum incidence degree and edge-connectivity is arbitrarily large. For adjacent vertices in any locally finite simple hypergraph, the Ollivier--Ricci idleness function is concave and piecewise affine with at most three affine pieces, and is affine on $[1/2,1]$. In particular, $\kappa_{\LLY}=2\kappa_{1/2}$, which we use to verify positive curvature in the two families of examples.
item.dc:creator: Qing Xia

item.title: Density of list- and correspondence-critical graphs
item.description: arXiv:2608.06757v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A graph $G$ is list $k$-critical if $G$ is not $(k-1)$-list-colorable, but every proper subgraph of $G$ is $(k-1)$-list-colorable. In this paper, we study the function $f_{\ell}(n,k)$ denoting the minimum number of edges in an $n$-vertex list $k$-critical graph, as well as the function $g_{\ell}(k) = \liminf_{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac 2n f_{\ell}(n,k) - k + 1$. We show that for all $k \geq 4$, every list $k$-critical graph on $n \geq k+2$ vertices has more than $(k-1+\frac 1{28})\frac n2$ edges, which implies that $g_{\ell}(k) \geq \frac{1}{28}$ for all $k \geq 4$. This is the first result showing that $\liminf_{k \rightarrow \infty} g_{\ell}(k) > 0$. We also show that $g_{\ell}(k) \geq \frac{1}{24}$ for all $k\geq 352$. As a corollary to our result, we obtain the following improvement to Brooks' theorem: For all $d \geq 3$, if $G$ has no $K_{d+1}$ subgraph and has maximum average degree at most $d+\frac 1{28}$, then $G$ is $d$-list-colorable. All of our results hold in the setting of correspondence coloring (DP-coloring) as well. As a corollary of our correspondence coloring result, we also show that for each $d \geq 3$, a minimal unsatisfiable anti-functional binary constraint satisfaction problem (CSP) with variable domains of size $d$ has a primal graph whose unique nontrivial component either contains $K_{d+1}$ or has average degree at least $d+\frac 1{28}$.
item.dc:creator: Peter Bradshaw

item.title: Disconnected graphs and extremal bounds for realizable distance orders
item.description: arXiv:2608.15853v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $G$ be a graph together with a total order $\prec$ on its edges. We say that $\prec$ is realizable in $\mathbb{R}^d$ if there is a placement of the vertices of $G$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ such that the Euclidean lengths of the edges induce exactly the order $\prec$. Almendra-Hern\'andez and Mart\'inez-Sandoval proved that every total order on the edges of the complete graph $K_n$ is realizable in $\mathbb{R}^{n-2}$. We show that the same is not true for the disjoint union of two complete graphs: for every $n\geq 3$ there is a total order on the edges of $K_n\sqcup K_n$ that is not realizable in $\mathbb{R}^{n-2}$, but is in $\mathbb{R}^{n-1}$. Thus, the realizability of an order on a disconnected graph is not determined by its restrictions to the connected components. We also study the extremal problem of maximizing the number of edges of an $n$-vertex graph all of whose edge-orders are realizable in $\mathbb{R}^d$, and show that for every fixed $d$ this maximum is $dn+o(n)$, with explicit bounds on the error term. On the real line we sharpen these bounds and show that a disjoint union of two cycles is realizable in $\mathbb{R}$ unless both cycles are triangles.
item.dc:creator: Gerardo L. Maldonado, Leonardo Mart\'inez-Sandoval, Miguel Raggi, Edgardo Rold\'an-Pensado

item.title: Cluster Geometry of Universal Schubert Polynomials I: Geometric Bases and Cluster Monomials
item.description: arXiv:2608.29125v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study Fulton's universal Schubert polynomials through the cluster structure on the upper unitriangular group and representations of type $A$. The convex hull of the initial tropical vectors of standard-elementary monomials is unimodularly equivalent to a product of simplices, and right-regular multisegments index three integral geometric bases of the standard-elementary module. A recursive prefix-record condition characterizes those universal Schubert polynomials that are homogeneous under diagonal conjugation, coincide with the corresponding generic and dual canonical basis elements, and are extended cluster monomials. On this locus, cover forests give squarefree factorizations into cluster variables. Outside it, the initial Laurent expansion has a coefficient $-1$.
item.dc:creator: Jiarui Fei

item.title: Turing universality, computability, and incompleteness in hypergraph Tur\'an theory
item.description: arXiv:2609.04295v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The hypergraph Tur\'an problem asks for the maximum asymptotic edge density of hypergraphs avoiding a forbidden family and the structure of near-extremizers. We prove that both encode arbitrary computation. Fix a universal Turing machine $\mathsf{U}$. For each fixed $r\ge3$, there is a rational $\tau_r\in(0,1)$ and an effective map from binary words $\beta$ to finite families $\mathcal{F}_{r,\beta}$ of $r$-graphs such that $\pi(\mathcal{F}_{r,\beta})=\tau_r$ if $\mathsf{U}$ does not halt on $\beta$, and $\pi(\mathcal{F}_{r,\beta})>\tau_r$ otherwise. For $r=3$, a single forbidden $3$-graph $P_\beta$ suffices. For all sufficiently large fixed $r$, we construct finite families exhibiting a parallel structural dichotomy. Nonhalting gives a unique extremal limit and edit-distance stability around a fixed finite profile. Halting yields 2 nonempty compact phases with opposite signs of a continuous statistic depending only on $r$; each phase is homeomorphic to the full extremal limit space of $P_\beta$. Hence uniqueness, connectedness, and finite-profile stability are undecidable. Our ZFC-verifiable reductions also yield independence results for every consistent computably axiomatized extension of ZFC, even for single forbidden $3$-graphs. We further classify the complexity of exact density comparison, characterize densities attainable by effectively enumerated families, and establish Busy-Beaver growth of minimal witnesses and the absence of computable positive lower bounds on density gaps.
item.dc:creator: Heng Li, Xizhi Liu

item.title: Sharp Bounds on the Number of Small Cuts
item.description: arXiv:2609.10255v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A $k$-cut of an undirected graph is a minimal edge set whose removal leaves at least $k$ connected components, and its cost is the sum of its edge costs. Write $\lambda_k$ for the minimum cost of a $k$-cut. For fixed $k\ge2$ and $\alpha\ge1$, we show that in any $n$-vertex graph with $n\ge k$ and nonnegative edge costs, the number of $k$-cuts of cost strictly below $\alpha\lambda_k$ is $O(n^{\lceil\alpha k\rceil-1})$. This implies an $O(n^{\lfloor\alpha k\rfloor})$ bound for $k$-cuts of cost at most $\alpha\lambda_k$, sharpening the $O(n^{\alpha k})$ bound of Gupta, Harris, Lee and Li. For $k=2$, our strict bound resolves a conjecture of Henzinger and Williamson and an open question of Karger. The exponent $\lceil\alpha k\rceil-1$ is optimal for $k$-cuts for every $k\ge2$ and $\alpha>1$.
item.dc:creator: Yu Cong, Chao Xu

item.title: Subset-Sum Density Realization in Locally Finite Abelian Groups
item.description: arXiv:2609.14630v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $G$ be a countable locally finite abelian group, and let \[ G_1\leq G_2\leq\cdots, \qquad \bigcup_{i\geq1}G_i=G, \] be any filtration of $G$ by finite subgroups. For $A\subseteq G$, let $\mathcal P(A)$ denote the set of all finite subset sums of elements of $A$, and let $2G:=\{2g:g\in G\}$. We prove that $|2G|=\infty$ if and only if for every filtration and every interval $[\alpha,\beta]\subseteq[0,1]$, there exists $A\subseteq G$ such that the set of limit points of \[ \left( \frac{|\mathcal P(A)\cap G_i|}{|G_i|} \right)_{i\geq1} \] is exactly $[\alpha,\beta]$. We also prove a positive-density result that does not require $|2G|=\infty$: if $G$ is infinite and $\mathcal P(A)$ has positive upper density along the given filtration, then there is an infinite set $B\subseteq \mathcal P(A)$ such that $B+B\subseteq \mathcal P(A)$. Combining this with the realization theorem, we show that, when $|2G|=\infty$, every interval $[\alpha,\beta]$ with $0\leq\alpha\leq\beta\leq1$ and $\beta>0$ can be realized by a set $A$ with this additional property.
item.dc:creator: Norbert Hegyv\'ari, Thang Pham, Boqing Xue

item.title: An Asymptotically Tight Bound on the Number of Distinct Squares in Circular Words
item.description: arXiv:2609.32084v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A square is a word $xx$ with $x$ nonempty. We study the maximum number of distinct squares occurring in the rotations of a word of length $n$. Amit and Gawrychowski (SPIRE 2017) obtained an upper bound of $3.14n$. Charalampopoulos et al. (CPM 2026) improved the upper bound to $\lceil9n/5\rceil$ and gave a binary construction with at least $3n/2-O(\sqrt n)$ distinct squares for infinitely many $n$. They conjectured an upper bound of $3n/2$. Li and Song subsequently reported an improved upper bound of $5n/3$.
