We prove that a circular word of length $n$ containing $\sigma$ distinct letters has at most $\lfloor3(n-\sigma)/2\rfloor$ distinct squares. This settles the conjecture and establishes that the leading coefficient $3/2$ is optimal even for binary words. Our proof groups squares by their Lyndon roots and, for primitive words, uses a weighted count of circuits in the Rauzy graphs of the bi-infinite repetition of the word.
item.dc:creator: Rikuya Hamai

item.title: Ehrhart Properties under Operations on Lattice Polytopes
item.description: arXiv:2610.06338v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper investigates the preservation of three classes of Ehrhart properties under various operations on lattice polytopes. These operations include Cartesian products, lattice joins, lattice pyramids, free sums, Minkowski sums, Cayley sums, reflexive polarity, and integral dilations. Specifically, we consider the following properties frequently studied in Ehrhart theory: (i): Positivity of Ehrhart coefficients, including Ehrhart positivity and magic positivity. In particular, we present lattice point counting formulas for the polytopes generated by these operations. (ii): Coefficient properties of the $h^*$-polynomial, including symmetry, unimodality, log-concavity, ultra log-concavity, real-rootedness, and $\gamma$-positivity. (iii): Geometric properties, including the spanning property, the integer decomposition property, very ampleness, and the existence of unimodular triangulation, regular unimodular triangulation, and quadratic triangulation. We determine which properties are preserved under these eight operations, establishing preservation theorems or constructing explicit counterexamples. Furthermore, when a property is not preserved in general, we investigate sufficient or equivalent conditions for its preservation.
item.dc:creator: Feihu Liu

item.title: Descartes' rule of signs for arbitrary fewnomial systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.06435v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The classical Descartes' rule of signs bounds the number of positive roots of a real polynomial in one variable by the number of sign changes of its coefficients. This bound only depends on the order of the exponents and on the signs of the coefficients, that is, on the oriented matroids of the exponent and coefficient matrices. We give a multivariate generalization of this rule to arbitrary fewnomial systems: for systems of $n$ real polynomial equations in $n$ variables with $n+k+1$ monomials, we obtain upper bounds for the number of nondegenerate positive solutions which only depend on sign conditions on the maximal minors of the coefficient matrix and of the exponent matrix and its liftings. For $k=1$ they are the Descartes rules of signs for circuits of Bihan--Dickenstein and Bihan--Dickenstein--Forsg{\aa}rd. Our approach starts from the Gale duality and the Khovanskii--Rolle argument of Bihan and Sottile, which reduce the problem to counting common zeros of iterated Jacobians in a polyhedron $\Delta$. This polyhedron is a chamber of a hyperplane arrangement whose combinatorics is determined by the oriented matroid of the coefficient matrix. We bound the number of these zeros by the B\'ezout number minus the zeros forced in the other chambers by a topological degree, which we compute by a facet-count formula involving the signs of minors of a Gale dual matrix of the exponent matrix. This leads to a recursion over the flats of the arrangement, which ends on lines with the Descartes rules for circuits. In this way the coefficients enter the bounds through the combinatorics of the arrangement, and the exponents through sign conditions on minors. Restricting the recursion to coherent chambers gives weaker bounds in closed form, which generalize the Descartes rule for circuits as ``the B\'ezout number minus the coherent chambers''.
item.dc:creator: Fr\'ed\'eric Bihan

item.title: $2$-Large Sets and Nil-Bohr Recurrence: A Disproof of the $2$-Large Is Large Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.16605v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A set $S$ of positive integers is $r$-large if every $r$-coloring of $\mathbb{N}$ contains arbitrarily long monochromatic arithmetic progressions with common difference in $S$. We prove that every $2$-large set is a set of nil-Bohr recurrence, i.e., it meets every nil-Bohr neighborhood of $0$. This proves a conjecture of the first author and gives a sharp answer to a question of Host, Kra, and Maass. Furthermore, we show that a piecewise syndetic set is $2$-large if and only if it is nil-Bohr recurrent. From this, we show that a small modification of a set constructed by the first author is $2$-large but not $3$-large, thereby disproving the $2$-large is large conjecture of Brown, Graham, and Landman. We also deduce that the family of $2$-large sets is not partition regular, thereby answering another question of Brown, Graham, and Landman. We also show that, for every fixed nil-Bohr neighborhood $B$ of $0$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, restricting the common difference to $B$ increases the extremal number for $k$-term arithmetic progressions by at most a factor of $1+\varepsilon$, provided $k$ is sufficiently large.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Alweiss, Sohail Farhangi

item.title: On separators in $K_h$-minor-free graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.40270v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This manuscript presents a proof of the Alon--Seymour--Thomas conjecture developed under the author's guidance using ChatGPT 6pro. More precisely, for every integer $h\geq3$, every $n$-vertex $K_h$-minor-free graph has a vertex set of size at most $16h\sqrt n$ whose deletion leaves every component with at most $2n/3$ vertices. The author has checked every formula and theorem by hand and used Codex to assist with writing (editing formulas, polishing the language, and typesetting). GPT 6.1 Sol (Max) was also used to check the proof repeatedly and to generate numerous examples for verification. The author takes full responsibility for the correctness of the proof.
item.dc:creator: Xinheng Lin

item.title: The Cranston--Li--Su--Wang--Xu (2026) conjecture is true
item.description: arXiv:2610.40863v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $A$ be a finite abelian group. A nowhere-zero $A$-flow of a graph can be changed along a cycle: going around the cycle, add a fixed non-zero element of $A$ to the value of every edge that points forward and subtract it from the value of every edge that points backward. The Cranston--Li--Su--Wang--Xu (2026) conjecture on the reconfiguration of nowhere-zero flows states that if $A$ has at least four elements, then in every graph in which all degrees are even, any two nowhere-zero $A$-flows are joined by a chain of such changes through nowhere-zero $A$-flows. It also states that, for every integer $k\ge 4$, the same holds for integer flows whose values are between $1$ and $k-1$ in absolute value, where each change adds a non-zero integer. We prove this conjecture. The proof is by induction on the number of edges. If a flow enters a vertex along one edge and leaves it along another edge with the same value, the two edges can be replaced by a single edge; this gives a smaller graph. The main step is to change every flow into a flow with such a pair of edges. For $A$-flows we do this when all degrees are at most $4$; repeatedly replacing a vertex of degree at least $6$ by a triangle, following Cranston et al., reduces the general case to this one. For integer flows, we show that, in a graph in which all degrees are even, any two nowhere-zero flows with values in the cyclic group $\mathbb{Z}_k$, $k\ge 4$, are joined by changes that add only $1$, $-1$, $2$ or $-2$, and that such changes lift to integer flows. All theorems of this paper are also proved in the Lean 4 proof assistant.
item.dc:creator: Dave Goel

item.title: Strong edge-colourings of truncations of cubic graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.41950v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a problem posed by Kardo\v{s} asking whether the truncation of every connected simple bridgeless cubic graph has strong chromatic index six. The truncation $T(G)$ is obtained by replacing each vertex of a graph $G$ with a triangle and attaching its three incident edges to distinct vertices of that triangle. Han and Cui established an affirmative answer for prism bases. We prove that the strong chromatic index is six whenever $G$ is a connected simple cubic graph that is bipartite or is both bridgeless and claw-free. Both proofs are constructive and use a common compatibility criterion for combining colourings of smaller pieces. The same equality holds for connected loopless cubic multigraphs in either class, with the sole exception of the $3$-bond, whose truncation is the triangular prism and has strong chromatic index nine.
item.dc:creator: Domenico Labbate, Federico Romaniello

item.title: A spectral Moore problem and the Yang-Koolen conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.00591v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the maximum order $v(k,\theta)$ of a connected $k$-regular graph whose second largest eigenvalue is at most $\theta$. For every real $\theta\geq1$, we prove that \[ T(\theta) =\limsup_{k\to\infty}\bigl(v(k,\theta)-2k\bigr) =2\left\lfloor1+\frac{\theta^2}{4}\right\rfloor. \] In particular, $T(\theta)>2\theta$ for every real $\theta\geq4$, disproving the Yang-Koolen conjecture. We also determine $v(k,\theta)$ for all sufficiently large $k$ on explicit intervals of $\theta$. We prove a jump in the second largest eigenvalue above $1$. For each fixed $1\leq\theta<2$ and all sufficiently large $k$, every connected $k$-regular graph of order at least $2k+2$ whose second largest eigenvalue is at most $\theta$ is the crown graph. For $\theta=\sqrt2$, we prove that $v(k,\sqrt2)=2k+2$ for every $k\geq13$. Finally, we give a new upper bound on $v(k,\theta)$.
item.dc:creator: Vishal Gupta

item.title: A linear edge bound for k-quasi-planar graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.01509v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the $k$-quasi-planar graph conjecture for topological drawings. For every integer $k\ge 2$, a simple graph on $n\ge 3$ vertices admitting a drawing with no $k$ pairwise crossing edges has at most $1056(k-1)^2(n-2)$ edges. Thus the number of edges is linear in $n$, with an explicit quadratic dependence on $k$. The result allows multiple crossings between the same pair of edges, including edges with a common endpoint. The proof uses the double of a sphere with boundary to represent graph edges by closed geodesics on a hyperbolic surface. The endpoints of geodesic lifts induce partial orders of width at most $k-1$. A stability bound for greedy chain partitions, together with a counting argument over a triangulation, gives the stated edge bound.
item.dc:creator: Ankan Sadhu

item.title: Infinite Generalized Sidon Sets with a Negative Answer to a Problem of Szemer\'edi
item.description: arXiv:2611.01871v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $A(x)=|A\cap[1,x]|$. For every integer $h\ge3$, every finite $B_h$ set $A_0\subseteq\mathbb N$, and every $0<c\le h^{-2/h}$, we construct an infinite $B_h$ set $A\subseteq\mathbb N$ containing $A_0$ such that $A(x)/x^{1/h}$ has upper limit $c$ and lower limit zero. This extends the range $0<c\le1/h$ obtainable from our first construction, which answered a question of Cilleruelo and Nathanson, later raised by O'Bryant, on the existence of a positive upper limit. For $h=3$, a positive upper limit disproves the assertion $A(x)=o(x^{1/3})$ in Szemer\'edi's Problem~186(d). The improved range follows from an integer lift of a modular construction of G\'omez Ruiz and Trujillo Solarte, with large gaps between sums of distinct $r$-element multisets for each fixed $1\le r<h$. These gaps ensure that successive blocks can be adjoined by translation while preserving the $B_h$ property. The same prescribed limits can be attained inside every set of asymptotic density one containing $A_0$. Separately, we construct $2^{\aleph_0}$ extensions of $A_0$ that are maximal among all $B_h$ subsets of $\mathbb N$, have the prescribed limits, and avoid any prescribed finite subset of $\mathbb N\setminus A_0$. These maximal extensions can be chosen so that $\sum_{a\in A}a^{-1/h}$ diverges arbitrarily slowly.
item.dc:creator: Guoqing Wang, Wenkai Yang

item.title: Non-log-concave $\tau$-polynomials of regular graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.11056v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For any simple graph $G$ of order $n$, write its chromatic polynomial in the rising factorial basis as $P(G,x)=\sum_{j=0}^{n}(-1)^{n-j}c_j(G)x^{\langle j\rangle}$, where $x^{\langle j\rangle}=\prod_{i=0}^{j-1}(x+i)$ for $j\ge1$ and $x^{\langle 0\rangle}=1.$ Brenti (1992) introduced the $\tau$-polynomial of $G$ and its augmented version, defined by $$\tau(G,x)=\sum_{j=0}^n c_j(G)x^j~~~\text{and}~~~\overline \tau(G,x)=\sum_{j=0}^n j!c_j(G)x^j.$$ He asked whether $\tau(G,x)$ is always real-rooted and whether the coefficient sequence of $\overline \tau(G,x)$ is always log-concave. In this paper, we prove that for every integer $d\ge4$, there exists an integer $h_d\ge3$ such that $c_2(G)^2<c_1(G)c_3(G)$ for every connected $d$-regular graph $G$ of girth at least $h_d$. For such graphs, the coefficient sequences of both polynomials fail log-concavity at $j=2$, and thus both polynomials have nonreal roots by Newton's inequalities. This gives counterexamples to both questions among connected regular graphs of arbitrarily large girth.
item.dc:creator: Meiqiao Zhang, Fengming Dong

item.title: The elliptic Hall algebra and the combinatorics of affine Springer fibers
item.description: arXiv:2611.14177v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For coprime positive integers $m,n$ and $k\ge1$, we study the symmetric functions $e_k[-X^{m,n}Y]\cdot1$ arising from the elliptic Hall algebra action. We identify their $\omega_X$-transforms with the normalized bigraded Frobenius characteristics computed by Boixeda Alvarez--Hameister--Ma for the torus-equivariant Borel--Moore homology of the positive parts of homogeneous affine Springer fibers. We introduce cyclic LLT polynomials and determine their monomial expansions, yielding explicit monomial formulas for these elliptic Hall algebra expressions in terms of cyclic parking functions. These results extend the affine Springer fiber identity and monomial formula of Carlsson--Mellit from integral slopes to arbitrary positive rational slopes.
item.dc:creator: Donghyun Kim, Jaeseong Oh

item.title: Annular Obstructions and Skew-Shape Block Identities
item.description: arXiv:2611.14506v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give three principal results on weighted order ideals, cluster coefficients, and block-statistic enumerators. First, in the rank-two annular exchange model, the frozen row $(2,-3)$ yields the specialized polynomial $1+q^2$, which is not unimodal. Its interpretation as a single-lamination counterexample to Theorem 14 of Kang, Lee and Lim (European Journal of Combinatorics, 2026) depends on identifying this row with the shear coordinates of a bridging curve in the same triangulation. We discuss this geometric correspondence using published annular examples; it is not established by the algebraic calculation or formalized in Lean. Second, the same polynomial fails log-concavity, and the frozen row $(1,-2)$ gives the full-support polynomial $1+2q+7q^2+10q^3+9q^4+4q^5+q^6$, likewise violating log-concavity. These calculations provide obstructions relevant to their Conjecture 1, subject to the same geometric identification. Third, for arbitrary finite skew Young diagrams, we prove the block-statistic identity of Kahane's Conjecture 4.7 (arXiv:2607.11225v2), using an explicit correction of the root convention. The proof uses commuting tableau-transfer matrices, a connected-block inverse kernel, and finite polynomial differential equations, with companion Lean 4/Mathlib formalizations. As a consequence, we obtain a bivariate block refinement that is coefficientwise nonnegative in $t-1$ after a common monomial shift in $q$.
item.dc:creator: Adam Til\`epe

item.title: Crystal Structure of Upper Cluster Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2309.08326v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct upper seminormal crystals on the $\mu$-supported tropical points of skew-symmetric cluster algebras from their exchange matrices. A generic potential provides an additive categorification in which boundary representations determine the Cartan matrices and generic ranks describe the crystal operators. Under frozen-Jacobi-finiteness and reachability, the raising operators lift to locally nilpotent derivations of the upper cluster algebra. For $\tau$-exact boundary pairs, these derivations give integrable actions of derived Kac--Moody algebras in characteristic zero. In particular, the associated Cartan matrices are positive semidefinite. When the generic characters form a basis, this basis is BK-biperfect and the $\tau$-exact crystals are normal. We also construct algebraic Tits actions and describe compatibly pointed biperfect bases through a coefficient graph. The theory is illustrated by classical and new examples.
item.dc:creator: Jiarui Fei

item.title: Zero-divisor algebras of graph functions: quantum caging, entangling routing and stochastic first-passage exclusion
item.description: arXiv:2311.11978v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show how algebraic constraints on weighted graphs yield exact localization and controlled transport in quantum and stochastic systems. Antisymmetrizing a noncommutative, nonassociative product of vertex functions defines a Lie bracket. For a specified Lie cobracket over commutative rings without nonzero $2$-torsion, compatibility holds if and only if products of distinct incident edge weights vanish. When the coefficient ring is a finite product of integral domains, the edges with nonzero weights in each component of the ring form a matching. These matchings are determined by the edge weights and need not coincide across the components. These matchings yield exact two-vertex caging in fixed quantum channels; separately specified channel-selective controls enable coherent routing and path--internal-state entanglement. For matching-supported stochastic jump rates, they enforce first-passage exclusion, while prescribed internal-state switching opens inaccessible paths and yields a singular weak-switching escape limit. The bracket--cobracket factorization identifies a common edge operator underlying quantum kinetic Hamiltonians and Markov generators, subject to distinct sign and positivity conditions. The algebra fixes the channel structure; controlled motion requires additional dynamical operations.
item.dc:creator: F\"ul\"op Bazs\'o

item.title: Quivers with Polynomial Identities
item.description: arXiv:2508.00662v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We provide a topological characterization of quivers whose path algebra satisfies a polynomial identity. This class includes the oriented cycle and acyclic quivers and, in the latter case, we describe the associated T-ideal. We introduce a generalization of Arnold's A-graded algebras, which we call locally A-graded algebras, and prove that they are also PI. We give an example of a quiver algebra satisfying a polynomial identity, even if the path algebra of the quiver does not.
item.dc:creator: Giovanni Cerulli Irelli, Javier De Loera Ch\'avez, Elena Pascucci

item.title: Approximation Algorithms for Matroid-Intersection Coloring with Applications to Rota's Basis Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2604.03735v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study algorithmic matroid intersection coloring. Given $k$ matroids on a common ground set $U$ of $n$ elements, the goal is to partition $U$ into the fewest number of color classes, where each color class is independent in all matroids. It is known that $2\chi_{\max}$ colors suffice to color the intersection of two matroids, $(2k-1)\chi_{\max}$ colors suffice for general $k$, where $\chi_{\max}$ is the maximum chromatic number of the individual matroids. However, these results are non-constructive, leveraging techniques such as topological Hall's theorem and Sperner's Lemma. We provide the first polynomial-time algorithms to color two or more general matroids where the approximation ratio depends only on $k$ and, in particular, is independent of $n$. For two matroids, we constructively match the $2\chi_{\max}$ existential bound, yielding a 2-approximation for the Matroid Intersection Coloring problem. For $k$ matroids we achieve a $(k^2-k)\chi_{\max}$ coloring, which is the first $O(1)$-approximation for constant $k$. Our approach introduces a novel matroidal structure we call a \emph{flexible decomposition}. We use this to formally reduce general matroid intersection coloring to graph coloring while avoiding the limitations of partition reduction techniques, and without relying on non-constructive topological machinery. Furthermore, we give a \emph{fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme} (FPRAS) for coloring the intersection of two matroids when $\chi_{\max}$ is large. This yields the first polynomial-time constructive algorithm for an asymptotic variant of Rota's Basis Conjecture. This constructivizes Montgomery and Sauermann's recent asymptotic breakthrough and generalizes it to arbitrary matroids.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Arndt, Benjamin Moseley, Kirk Pruhs, Chaitanya Swamy, Michael Zlatin

item.title: Tree-Based Formalization of Multi-Agent Complementarity in Human-AI Interactions
item.description: arXiv:2606.04779v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Predictive tasks constitute subprocedures within human--AI interactions (HAIs) involving professionals and AI systems. Complementarity occurs when an HAI outperforms a benchmark defined by its constituent agents. Existing formalizations, however, focus on a single human and a single AI, leaving multi-agent interactions insufficiently characterized. We introduce a tree-based mathematical framework for multi-agent complementarity. Ordered agent-role configurations decorate the leaves of rooted planar binary trees and local aggregation rules generate protocol outputs evaluated against either a best-average or a pointwise-min benchmark. We establish four results. First, under linear pooling, every protocol tree provides a bijective coordinate system for the interior of the simplex of global leaf weights. Arbitrary trees with the same ordered leaves admit output- and complementarity-preserving reparameterizations, realized locally through path-independent Tamari rotations. However, HAI constraints can violate admissibility preservation between equivalent protocols. Second, for regression under squared loss, we characterize complementarity through residual correction and derive optimal linear-pooling weights. We also characterize protocol-indifference loci under identical local parameters. Third, selector-based protocols cannot achieve complementarity relative to the pointwise-min benchmark, independently of task and loss. Fourth, in binary classification, HAIs cannot achieve complementarity under endpoint-monotone losses and the pointwise-min benchmark, with an analogous obstruction for multiclass cross-entropy. Numerical illustrations examine the main claims. We provide a mathematical foundation for analyzing multi-agent predictive subprocedures within HAIs, establishing a first step toward understanding how interaction, aggregation, and real-world constraints affect HAI performance.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Ferrario

item.title: Power-integral matrices over number fields: the Drazin inverse, pseudo-determinant, and numerical semigroups
item.description: arXiv:2606.30876v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate matrices with entries in a number field such that some positive power has all its entries in the corresponding ring of integers. Our work generalizes previous results in several directions and we find applications to numerical semigroups.
item.dc:creator: Theo Chinn, Junshu Feng, Stephan Ramon Garcia, Hechun Zhang

item.title: Two-Sided Dimension Bounds for the Peterson Hit Problem via Projections and Matrix Minors
item.description: arXiv:2608.02623v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mathcal P_k=\mathbb F_2[x_1,\ldots,x_k]$, with $\deg x_i=1$, be the polynomial algebra equipped with the standard unstable action of the mod-$2$ Steenrod algebra $\mathcal A$. The Peterson hit problem asks for a minimal homogeneous set of $\mathcal A$-generators for $\mathcal P_k$, or equivalently for a homogeneous basis of the cohit space $Q\mathcal P_k=\mathcal P_k/\mathcal A^+\mathcal P_k = \mathbb F_2\otimes_{\mathcal A}\mathcal P_k$, where $\mathcal A^+ $ denotes the augmentation ideal of $\mathcal A$. The dimension of $(Q\mathcal P_k)_d$ therefore gives the number of generators required in positive degree $d$. Although solved in every degree $d$ for $k\leq 4,$ the problem remains open in general. As the number of variables $k$ and degrees $d$ increase, exact calculations involve increasingly large systems of Steenrod relations. Motivated by this difficulty, in this work, we establish explicit upper and lower bounds for $\dim_{\mathbb F_2}(Q\mathcal P_k)_d$ for arbitrary positive integers $k$ and $d$. Our method combines binary combinatorics and linear algebra with graph-theoretic and simplicial structures in the matrix of the generating Steenrod squares.
item.dc:creator: Dang Vo Phuc, Peter V. Danchev

item.title: Isometric embeddings of trees: why 32 leaves can require six dimensions, and bounds for every tree
item.description: arXiv:2608.16288v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We identify the first failure of the $\lceil\log_2 t\rceil$ leaf-count bound for isometric embeddings of $t$-leaf trees under the maximum norm. Every tree with at most $31$ leaves attains the bound, but a $32$-leaf tree requires six dimensions. This answers a question of Fitzpatrick and Nowakowski and disproves a conjecture of Aksoy, K{\i}l{\i}\c{c} and Ko\c{c}ak. We explain this failure by showing how requirements within and between branches force an additional coordinate. For a family of three-branch trees, we prove that the leaf bound is attained exactly when the two larger branches have equal leaf counts; otherwise, one additional coordinate is necessary. We also prove that every tree embeds in $\lceil 1.162832\log_2 t\rceil$ dimensions, improving the coefficient of approximately $1.44042$ established in 2005. These results hold for arbitrary positive edge lengths and the entire metric realization. We also construct infinite families in which the excess persists under repeated leaf expansion. Both main theorems are formalised in Lean using only standard axioms.
item.dc:creator: Logan R. Chalmers

item.title: Fence Posets, Good Gradings and Frobenius Maximal Parabolics
item.description: arXiv:2609.10869v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mathfrak L$ be a Frobenius maximal parabolic subalgebra of $\mathfrak{sl}_n$. For any $F\in\mathfrak L^*$ for which the Kirillov form $B_F(x,y)=F([x,y])$ is non-degenerate, let $\widehat F$ denote the associated principal element. We prove that the multiplicities of the eigenvalues of $\operatorname{ad}_{\widehat F}$ on $\mathfrak L$ form a unimodal sequence symmetric about $\frac12$. We also prove that the multiplicities of the eigenvalues of $\operatorname{ad}_{\widehat F}$ on $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ form a unimodal sequence symmetric about $0$. The proof relates the ranked meander associated to $\mathfrak L$ to the order ideals of a related fence poset through Panyushev reduction. The known unimodality of the rank polynomial of the fence poset implies that of the meander, which in turn determines a good grading of $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ in the sense of Elashvili and Kac. We prove that this grading coincides with that induced by the principal element and that the pyramid associated to this grading may be filled in such a way that its good element $e$ lies in $\mathfrak L$. The two unimodality results then follow from the injectivity properties of $\operatorname{ad}_e$ coming from the good grading and the duality induced by the bilinear form $B_F$.
item.dc:creator: Anthony Giaquinto, John Irving, Aaron Lauve, Mitja Mastnak

item.title: The existence and uniqueness of magic-faced hypercubes, and applications to Khajuraho most-perfect magic squares, cubes, and hypercubes
item.description: arXiv:2609.26762v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A $\textit{magic-lined hypercube}$ (or, simply, $\textit{magic hypercube}$) of order $k$ and dimension $n$ is an arrangement of the numbers $1,\dots,k^n$ in a $k\times\cdots\times k$ ($n$-fold) grid such that every line of $k$ numbers parallel to a coordinate axis has the same magic sum. While such hypercubes exist for every order $k\ge 3$ and every dimension $n$, no magic-lined hypercube of order $2$ exists in any dimension $n\ge 2$. For hypercubes of order $2$, we thus relax the magic condition from lines to two-dimensional faces or planes. We call an arrangement of the numbers $1,\dots,2^n$ in a $2\times\cdots\times2$ ($n$-fold) grid \emph{magic-faced} if every $2\times2$ face has the same magic sum. We prove that a magic-faced hypercube of order $2$ exists in every dimension $n\ge0$, and that it is unique up to a certain natural set of transformations of size $2^n(n+1)!$ when $n$ is even and $2^n n\cdot n!$ when $n$ is odd. As an application, we recover and generalize the classical $4\times4$ Khajuraho magic square, give a new, conceptual answer to a question of Coxeter on the group acting on the $384$ ``most-perfect" $4\times4$ magic squares, and extend the picture to higher dimensions. In particular, we prove that, in dimension $n$, these most-perfect hypercubes form a single orbit under a certain natural action of the Weyl group $W(B_{2n})$.
item.dc:creator: Manjul Bhargava

item.title: A zero-one law for swap-invariant events in uniform spanning forests
item.description: arXiv:2610.00938v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that every event invariant under swaps has probability zero or one for either the free or the wired spanning forest on any connected, locally finite, infinite network. Applications include the constancy of the number of components and of the total number of excessive ends. For the free forest, these results resolve longstanding questions of Benjamini, Lyons, Peres, and Schramm [Ann. Probab. (2001), Question 15.7] on constancy of the component count and of Lyons, Morris, and Schramm [Electron. J. Probab. (2008), Question 7.7] on the zero-one law for one-endedness. In the latter case, we obtain the stronger conclusion that the total number of excessive ends is deterministic.
item.dc:creator: Xinyi Li, Yao Yu

item.title: K-unstable Toric Varieties and Secondary Polytopes
item.description: arXiv:2610.05179v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For a K-unstable toric variety, Sz\'ekelyhidi's optimal test-function $\Theta_{P}$ is a mysterious concave function over the moment polytope $P$, which gives the maximal destabilizer for K-stability, and encodes the limiting behavior of the divergent Calabi flow. As balanced norms quantize cscK metrics, we show that $\Theta_{P}$ can be quantized by the maximal destabilizers for Chow-stability, which are given by the shortest GKZ vectors, i.e., the least norm point on the secondary polytope associated to the set $P\cap k^{-1}\mathbb{Z}^{n}$. The proof is via the $\Gamma$-convergence method. Properties and algorithms for general sGKZ vectors are given. It may provide a new method to detect the K-instability of Delzant polytopes.
item.dc:creator: Chi Li, Li Sheng, Yi Yao

item.title: Log-concavity and unimodality of cluster monomials in fan coordinates of type A_n
item.description: arXiv:2610.09312v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that every cluster monomial of type A_n is log-concave and unimodal with respect to its Laurent expansion in a fan initial cluster. We derive a coefficient formula for laminar interval products arising from compatible diagonals in the polygon model. This gives partial affirmative answers to the log-concavity conjecture of Chen-Huang-Sun and the unimodality conjecture of Chen. Our result for cluster A-varieties also complements Shen's study on the supports of products of canonical basis elements for cluster X-varieties of type A_n.
item.dc:creator: Zhichao Chen

item.title: Sharp spherical $L^p\to L^4$ extension estimates over finite fields in odd dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.29664v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $q$ be an odd prime power, let $d\ge3$ be odd, and let $S_j=\{\xi\in \mathbb F_q^d:\xi_1^2+\cdots+\xi_d^2=j\}$, where $j\ne 0$. We prove the sharp extension estimate ${L^{4(d+1)/(3d+1)}(S_j, d\sigma)\to L^4(\mathbb F_q^d,dc)}$ whenever $\eta_q((-1)^{(d-1)/2}j)=-1$, where $\eta_q$ is the quadratic character. This confirms the odd-dimensional spherical extension conjecture of Koh, Pham, and Vinh over every finite field of odd characteristic. Together with the known estimate in the complementary sign class, this determines the sharp ${L^p\to{L^4}}$ extension range for all nonzero-radius spheres in odd dimensions. We also apply the endpoint estimate to obtain sufficient conditions for the unique recovery of sparse signals from incomplete Fourier data.
item.dc:creator: Thang Pham, Boqing Xue

item.title: Asymptotic Rank of Weighted Graph Tensors via Completely Positive Bounds
item.description: arXiv:2610.34273v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give a conic upper bound on the asymptotic rank of every weighted graph tensor over every field. If $W$ is the logarithmic edge-weight matrix of its dimension matrix $Q$, then $$ \operatorname{MaxCut}(W)\le\log_2\operatorname{\widetilde R}_{\mathbb F}(\mathsf{WT}(Q))\le U_{\operatorname{CP}}^{\Delta}(W). $$ Here $U_{\operatorname{CP}}^{\Delta}(W)$ maximizes $\sum_{1\le i<j\le n}W_{i,j}P_{i,j}$ over nonnegative symmetric zero-diagonal matrices $P$ such that $J-2P$ is copositive and $P_{i,j}\le P_{i,k}+P_{k,j}$ for all distinct vertices. The matrix $J$ is all-one, and copositivity means nonnegativity of the quadratic form on nonnegative vectors. Our starting point extends OpenAI's polynomial multiplication method and its subsequent arbitrary-field developments from three tensor legs to arbitrary order. We prove $$ \left\lfloor\frac{n^2}{4}\right\rfloor\le\log_2\operatorname{\widetilde R}_{\mathbb F}(\mathsf{GT}_2(K_n))\le\frac{n^2}{4}. $$ The edge exponent is at most $n/(2(n-1))$ and tends to the optimal value $1/2$, improving the previous Coppersmith--Winograd bounds and answering Question 1.3.1 of Christandl, Vrana, and Zuiddam. The bounds coincide for every even $n$. For every odd $m\ge3$, the theorem gives $\log_2\widetilde R_{\mathbb F}(\mathsf{GT}_2(C_m))\le m-1+1/(m+1)$, improving the previous cycle bound with a gap of only $1/(m+1)$ above the maximum cut. On weighted triangles, the program recovers the rectangular matrix multiplication curve of Uzna'nski and Amanov, van den Berg, and Zuiddam. The CP and semidefinite programs, with or without path constraints, all have value $9/4$ on the unweighted triangle, giving this upper bound a natural conic interpretation. Further applications give explicit bounds for complete multipartite graphs, split graphs, and wheels, including new cases of maximum-cut equality.
item.dc:creator: Huanyi Zhou

item.title: Geometric progressions in distance sets in odd dimensions over prime fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.34758v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For $E\subset\mathbb{F}_p^d$, let $\Delta(E)=\{Q_d(x-y):x,y\in E\}$, where $Q_d(z)=z_1^2+\cdots+z_d^2$. We introduce and study the problem of the existence of nondegenerate three-term geometric progressions in the distance set $\Delta(E)$ when $d$ is odd. Let $M_{GP,d}(p)$ be the largest size of a set whose distance set contains no such progression. For every prime $p\geq7$ and every integer $m\geq0$, we prove \[ p^mM_{GP,1}(p)\leq M_{GP,2m+1}(p) \leq4p^mM_{GP,1}(p). \] For all sufficiently large primes $p$, we also prove \[ p^{m+\frac{7}{26}}\leq M_{GP,2m+1}(p) \leq Cp^{m+\frac{16}{25}}, \] where $C$ is an absolute positive constant.
item.dc:creator: Thang Pham, Dung The Tran, Boqing Xue

item.title: Hodge--Riemann relations for nef bundles
item.description: arXiv:2610.37650v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce the $(m,p,q)$-Lefschetz property for $(1,1)$-type endomorphisms of Hodge--Lefschetz modules, providing a framework for studying nef $(1,1)$-classes and characteristic classes of nef vector bundles on compact K\"ahler manifolds. Under a Hall--Rado type condition on nef twisted vector bundles, we prove Hodge--Riemann relations for products of top Chern classes and, in suitable bidegrees, for products of derived Schur classes. For products of nef $(1,1)$-classes, we show furthermore that the Hall--Rado type condition is equivalent to simultaneous Hodge--Riemann relations. Our proofs build on the purity theorem and descent lemma of Cattani, Kaplan, and Schmid. We extend the descent lemma to Schur classes of nef vector bundles. We also establish formal analogs for projective bundle modules over Hodge--Lefschetz modules, with applications to tautological classes and descent on matroid Chow rings.
item.dc:creator: Enhan Li, Weizhe Zheng

item.title: Generalized Discrete Fractal Dimensions of Graph Families
item.description: arXiv:2610.39187v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study generalized discrete fractal dimensions of sequences of finite connected graphs whose diameters tend to infinity. Using normalized shortest-path metrics and a general scale function, we define regularized energy dimensions for vertex probability measures and their optimized versions. We then establish a variational principle that identifies the optimized energy dimension with the supremum of ball-mass concentration dimensions. We also establish monotonicity in the moment order, stability under uniformly comparable measures, and upper bounds in terms of R\'enyi entropy growth and the upper mass dimension. Cluster estimates and explicit graph constructions show that local vertex concentration can lower the uniform energy dimension without changing the mass dimension. Finally, for uniformly Ahlfors-regular graph families, we obtain an integral criterion for energy boundedness and explicit formulas for the critical dimensions. These results clarify how global growth, local distance distributions, and the choice of scale function jointly determine discrete fractal dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Jiantao Liu, Cheng Zeng, Yumei Xue, Qingcheng Zeng

item.title: Ideals of 2-minors of nearly determinantal matrices
item.description: arXiv:2611.06571v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Motivated by the study of prime binomial ideals with Cohen--Macaulay quotients and linear resolutions, we introduce nearly determinantal matrices, a class of matrices obtained by repeating variables from the preceding rows in the last row. We characterize the primality of their ideals of $2$-minors in terms of an associated directed graph with row labels. For every prime case, we prove that the quotient is a normal Cohen--Macaulay domain and determine its graded Betti numbers. Finally, a prime ideal in this family has a linear resolution if and only if the matrix has three rows or two columns.
item.dc:creator: Takayuki Hibi, Francesco Navarra, Ayesha Asloob Qureshi

item.title: Resolving Tusn\'ady's Problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.06998v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove a lower bound of $\Omega_d((\log N)^{d-1/2})$ for the worst-case combinatorial discrepancy of $N$-point sets with respect to anchored boxes in every fixed dimension $d\ge3$. Together with Nikolov's upper bound of the same order and Wei's planar lower bound, this settles Tusn\'ady's problem: the discrepancy of axis-parallel boxes is $\Theta_d((\log N)^{d-1/2})$ in every fixed dimension $d\ge2$. The proof combines smoothed product test functions, sampling discretization, and an entropy argument for conditioned Gaussian vectors. The matching upper and lower bounds are also formalized in Lean 4.
item.dc:creator: Nicola Wengiel

item.title: Annular webs and Guralnick's conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.09114v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Using annular webs and Kazhdan-Lusztig mu-coefficients, we disprove Guralnick's absolute boundedness conjecture for first cohomology.
item.dc:creator: Tom Goertzen, Abel Lacabanne, Daniel Tubbenhauer, Pedro Vaz

item.title: Linear structure graphs associated with commuting graphs of Lie algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.10788v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The commuting graph (CG) of a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over a field of characteristic zero forgets the linear structure, and a non-trivial center creates redundant vertices. We introduce linear structure graphs (LSGs), whose vertices are the nonzero vectors of a vector space and whose edge set is stable under linear operations. Each vertex generates a finite ascending sequence of subspaces, which defines its LSG-height; this height governs connectivity. We characterize LSGs of height at most 1 and show that the CG of a Lie algebra with trivial center has height at most 1 if and only if the algebra is a commutative transitive Lie algebra (CTLA). The reduced commuting graph (RCG) restricts the CG to a complement of the center; it is well defined up to LSG-isomorphism, preserves the connectivity, diameter and number of components of the CG, and is compatible with direct sums. Finally, we characterize almost abelian Lie algebras (AALAs) by their RCGs.
item.dc:creator: Vu A. Le, Hoa Q. Duong, Tuan A. Nguyen
